If you're looking for a game review you've come to the wrong place. But if youre looking for a fantastic ravioli recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients
- To Make the Dough
375 grams (3 cups) plain flour
1/2 teaspoon salt
2 eggs
1/4 cup (50 ml / 3½ tablespoons) olive oil
1/2 cup (120 ml / 8 tablespoons) water
Extra flour for dusting
- To Make Cheese Filling
15 ounces (425 grams) container Ricotta cheese
5 ounces (142 g/about 1/2 cup plus 2 tablespoons) "3 Cheese Italian Blend" (Parmesan, Romano & Asiago)
Note: grate these cheeses yourself and create your own custom blend.
1/2 cup cheddar cheese
2 eggs, lightly beaten
1/2 teaspoon salt
1/2 teaspoon pepper
- Extras
Your favorite sauce for the ravioli (i.e. marinara/ marijuana)
Parmesan cheese
Basil
Fried vegetables
Shrimp
Fish slices
Chicken pieces
Make the Ravioli filling.
cinnamon
- In a small mixing bowl, add the ricotta and mash with a fork.
- Add in the 3-cheese blend, Cheddar cheese, eggs, salt, and pepper.
- Mix all ingredients thoroughly until you have a smooth, paste-like consistency.
- Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and place it in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
Make the Ravioli dough.
- Crack eggs into a large mixing bowl and beat them with a fork. Add water, oil, and salt. Mix.
- Add 1 cup flour to the bowl. Use a fork to mix the flour with the eggs, water, oil, and salt. Repeat with the rest of the flour. Mix until a smooth dough is formed.
- Clear and clean off a large work surface and dust it with flour. This is where you are going to roll out your dough.
- Take the dough out of the mixing bowl, shape it into a ball, and place it on your work surface. Knead for at least 10 minutes or until it becomes elastic.
- Dust a rolling pin with flour to prevent the dough from sticking. Roll out the dough until it is about 1/8 inch (1/3 cm) thick, or about the thickness of 2 stacked quarters.
- With a cookie cutter or upside-down water glass, cut out circles in the dough (will make about 15-20 dough circles).
- Ball up the unused dough and either roll it out and make a couple more raviolis, or wrap it and put in the freezer for another time. Dough can keep for weeks when frozen. Just make sure to wrap well so that it doesn’t suffer from freezer burn or absorb freezer odor.
Fill the Ravioli shells.
- Take the ravioli filling out of the refrigerator and place a tablespoon of it in middle of a dough.
- Fill a small bowl with water, dip your fingers in, and moisten around the outer edge of the dough circle.
- Fold the dough in half over the filling, making a half-moon shape. Be sure all the filling stays inside. Pinch the edges together and then seal the edges of the ravioli with a fork. Make sure to press firmly and go all the way around. This will add a “homemade” touch as well.
- Repeat this process for all your dough circles.
- Dust the finished ravioli with flour to keep them from sticking together.
Form the Shells and Fill Using a Ravioli maker.
- Roll the dough into two sheets
- Place one sheet on the ravioli maker, and form the filling cups.
- Fill with the ravioli mixture.
- Lay the second sheet of dough on top, and roll it out. This will seal in the filling.
- Remove and separate the finished raviolis.
Cook the Ravioli.
- Fill a large pot with water and bring to a boil.
- Place the ravioli in boiling water for 5-6 minutes, or until they float. You can also test for doneness by nibbling on the edges to test.
- If you don't want to make all the ravioli at one time, you can freeze the rest
- Take ravioli out of boiling water with large slotted spoon and place on warmed plates
Serve it up.
Top with your favorite sauce, grate some fresh cheese over it, and enjoy!

This sequel drops you right where the first game ended. Agent 47's Russian uncle goes through a PTSD-like dream which conjures up many of the deeds he has carried out as a SMERSH agent. Making the lack of emotion emanating from Hitman's colder-blooded protagonist all the more understandable, for continuity's sake that is...
On a more serious note,
features better graphics, slightly more comfortable gameplay mechanics, and manages to become immersive up to a certain extent (both environment and soundtrack-wise). Nazi imagery isn't ridiculously censored anymore, and although this isn't of the utmost importance, it still constitutes a little plus in my book. Oh and you can also switch the voice-acting to its' original Russian version.
The only downside I can think of is the length of this game. Which is considerably shorter than the first outing. Needless to say, you'll still waste plenty of time looking for this-or-that oddity which may (or may not) confer a tremendous advantage over your prey. You get a fair variety of locations and situations.
All in all, I enjoyed this game much more than the former, more rugged
. I'd highly recommend this game for those of you who are unhappy with the course the Hitman franchise has taken, you'll possibly find solace in this gem.

The developers have abandoned this game. They will not be adding new content. They said that they will patch the bugs but the last patch was 3 months ago. The bug list in the last patch was pages long ( even though they call this version of the game 2.0 when it is actually closer to 0.8 )
I mean only a dumba** or a conman, or a poor coder calls an unfinished game "finished". Within the game, they advertise another game that they currently working on... I've read that the developers worked on Prison Architect for 6 years and are bored / tired of the game.
I bought this game for $5 during a fire sale ( summer 2015 ). Back then, I figured that the developers were having financial problems developing the game. Back then, my viewpoint was that I was buying into an early access game that may or may be finished.
My overall rating for this game is 80% - it can be very absorbing but the bugs and glitches sap the joy from the game. You will have to alt-tab and search the Internet for solutions to bugs in the campaign. Even if all the bugs in the game were fixed, without additional content, this game would probably rate no higher than 83%.
Prisoners will punch objects. The game sometimes glitches and inadvertently blocks you from repairing and interacting with the object at all. This causes huge problems; you end up with physical obstacles like doors, that you have to work around and it causes knockon problems with the AI acting like a spaz ( I've seen workers and janitors chase one another, congregate in a circle and hump each other, like dogs in heat, in an outdoor orgy ). Another thing that infuriates me is that sometimes I will build and furnish a cell and the game will say that it's not a valid cell because it has be, "surrounded by walls and a door" ( the game can't figure out something that the average 5 year old child could figure out ). Sometimes the game will place prisoners in the "invalid" cell and not give me credit for building the f* thing or sometimes the game won't use the cell at all, at which point I wasted time and money ( which aptly sums up this game ).
Another dumb thing is that the game rewards you for prisoners dying; in the form of receiving cash subsidies for taking in new prisoners. You could probably make a lucrative business by killing off the inmates. It's a lot easier than having the inmates working to produce manufactured goods because they only work when they feel like it ( which is hardly ever, unless they want to use the opportunity to escape ).
The game is a massive time sink. It takes hours just to do things because you are so cash-screwed. You just sit back and watch the clock tick, watch the prisoners and staff, sometimes micromanage fights between staff and inmates. The game features a fast foward button - that's how empty the game is. Almost every city building game features random events but those barely exist in this game ( lazy coders ).
If you are a hardcore gamer, it is really not worth your time to struggle against the bugs, since there are better games in the same genre.

This game is a charming metroidvania that I can reccomend to many, but it does have it's flaws.
-Ori's control is tight
-plenty of progressive upgrades that eventually give you plenty of options and mobility
-the visuals are stunning
-I'v had little trouble backtracking in this game, which is impressive for a game like this.
-the music is good
-You don't need a guide to 100% this game. (perhaps not the achievements, some of them can be really tough)
-this is the main flaw for me, the difficulty curve of this game seems to be having a stroke, in one moment you're exploring vast areas enjoying the sights, and the next you're caught off guard by a ton of insta-death hazards that can rival super meat boy.
-the controls get a tad bit more complex by the end of the game since it seems every single button on the controller is used for something.
-the music may be good but it's forgettable
-sometimes there is little guidance as to what you're supposed to do, but that may be a pro to some.
-the combat seems to be a bit lacking, but you do feel quite powerful at the end of the game.
-some of the insta-death hazards can't be spotted until it's too late
Overall this is a great game, but do expect to die a lot.

Then you fight him later where he does the same attacks, so the game just had us fight the same boss twice.  I also like to achievement hunt, and I think that multiplayer achievements are an abomination.  I think a lot of the work that could have gone into the single player story of the game instead went into making the multiplayer. I encountered a bug where Batman gets stuck in a nightclub, which can't be fixed by reloading/ restarting the game.  I looked for anyone else who had this problem, and there was a post from TWO YEARS AGO where people also had the same problem.  I had noticed a few minor bugs either in combat or weird flying patterns, which weren't a big deal.  However if the developer can't patch a huge bug like the one I encountered in two whole years, I get the feeling they don't care about their customers.

Taking a step forward deep into the chaotic endless black desert of insanity.
Max Payne 2 eventhough it stands on common ground it really has many differences from its predecessor.
Something that made the hard core fans of the first game not like it too much at first.
However for me Max Payne 2 really stands out of the library and into my golden list of masterpieces and on the throne with the rest of my most fav titles ever.
The game has obvious graphical advancements engine-wise, physics-wise, texture-wise and gameplay-wise.
The environmental design stays along the lines of the same dark concept the first game was in and goes deep in the underground paths of life of a world filled with corruption.
The design and overall direction gets you straight into the mood of a romance/mafia-drama with strong storytelling elements, incredible naration and amazing voice acting.
The character models are completelly different from the first game. I really really loved Timothy Gibbs for Max and Kathy Tong for Mona.
Also the gameplay is really smooth, easier to survive compared to the first game mechanism-wise, smarter AI, better slo-mo bullettime feature, better gun design and scripting.
What impressed me most about this game is the movie-like quality of the naration and the perfectly scripted quotes in it.
The game feels like a dramatic movie that sucks you down to its darkness which bewitches you to not wanna get out.
Transforming the line into a blur to what's black or white, what's good or bad, what's life or death, the unique experience of following Max Payne through the events of the game leaved me beyond satisfied.
The game also supports mods, and there are tons out there, which increases its replayability value.
Glad to have played this game for once more and totally recommending and urging you all who haven't, to buy this asap and play it now. Especially if you are into action/mafia genre games with a strong taste of Noir Drama.

Death to Spies: Moment of Truth is probably my favorite stealth game, next to Splinter Cell: Chaos Theory and Hitman: Blood Money.
Every level is incredibly unique among the seven few that there are, but the game gives you just enough tools and varied enough difficulty levels (the difference between the hard difficulty and the hardest difficulty is alone practically two seperate games) that the lack of quantity barely effects the game.
Tossable, infinite distractions, with more limited more focused variants. Whistling to distract. Three stances with two movement speeds between them. Usable vehicles (with usable horns.)
Accident systems.
At least one level with a straight up logistics puzzle.
Oh, and really solid, clockwork inspired music.
Most impressively, easy difficulty has more spaced out patrols and scripted lures that don't exist on other difficulties, ensuring that even novices have more than a fair chance to understand the workings of the game.
This isn't for people who want a story with their game. Frankly, this isn't for people who want anything but a raw, enjoyable set of levels that end up being fun to play through.
The animations aren't the best, nor is the plot anything amazing, and the combat AI isn't fantastic. That said, if you're picking this up the odds are you're not looking for any of those things.
If you like stealth for stealth's sake, this is easily one of the best games you can pick up on Steam.
It's the expansion pack Hitman: Blood Money never got, and you owe it to yourself to pick it up.

An amazing and vastly underrated gem for those looking for a Hitman type genre with a realistic story and depth.  NPC AI is very intuitive and boasts some personality—they are quick to catch on when something is amiss, To fool them will take practiced skill, patience, and a lot of game-saves. This is Splinter Cell meets Hitman, meets the original COD.
One thing Death to Spies is not, is a full blown FPS—the AI breaks down once a full on fire-fight ensues and the game mechanics simply aren’t suited for intense action. You may fire the occasional shot, but you'll mainly be sneaking around, collecting, quietly assassinating, sabotaging, poisoning, and changing your cloths often to avoid detection and gain access to restricted areas.
Aesthetically, the graphics and sound quite good for the day — more than sufficient to create a compelling, immerse atmosphere where hours will pass. And although your objectives are clearly laid out, you'll find a moderately high replay value here, where you can go about your mission in a variety of ways.

I'd have to rate this game as an 8/10, although I wouldnt recommend it for the gameplay.  When it comes to the gameplay, just think of if you took Gears of War into a modern warfare setting.  Solid, but nothing much to distinguish it.  Where this game really comes alive is in the story and the setting.
The city of Dubai, still opulent and beautiful despite covered by the raging sandstorm ocurring int he background, is a highly unique environment for this game.  I cant say I've seen anything similar in other games.  When you walk through what appeared to be a plain of sand, only to fall into the top floor of a skyscraper, it is veyr incredible.  And even if this game came out a few years ago, it is still very beautiful.  The addition of adding a filter on top of the normal brightness setting means you can customize it in an interesting manner.  I went with brightness at about a 1/4 of the bar, with the vibrant feature.
The games story and the choices presented are the best part of this.  None of the choices here are forced (Unless you choose to just stand by and wait for the event to pass), but you find yourself drawn to making these terrible decisons.  It can make even the most gung ho kill'em all shooter player feel a bit unsettled about their actions, especially since this game doesn't shy away from showing the consequences of those actions.  The ending is quite interesting, although you'll have to have a keen sense of whats going on and pay attention in order to get the full story.  Easily one of the most interesting stories a shooter has tried.
Great game overall for if you want a game with some decent story and action to keep you busy in a night.

NMRiH, No More Room in Hell, is a survival horror modification game that is now a stand-alone version of a previous Half Life 2 mod. At first glance, the one interesting aspect that caught my eye about this particular zombie shooter was its captivating vintage-like post-apocalyptic atmosphere that's mainly to be praised because of the source engine used similar to HL:2's engine. I instantly felt a surge of nostalgia upon playing one of the game's objective-based maps titled Cabin; I felt a resemblance to Resident Evil Zero's Gamecube stylized graphics that led me into further enjoying the game for its aesthetic appeal.
In terms of the game's battle mechanics, I enjoyed the melee based combat system in which certain weaponry has its own stamina based consumption use and weight capacity. For example, the sledgehammer in the game uses an inordinate amount of stamina for the user but certainly compensates for the lack of swings you can hit with by substituting it with hard hitting zombie brain splattering fun one-hitters, which causes area of effect damage to multiple zombies! The weapons held within the game are scarce and thus preservation of ammunition is vital to one's success within the game, as well as the type of weapon used (certain weapons have paritcular uses for certain situations).
As previously mentioned, the game does hold objective based maps, up to a total of 5 objective oriented maps, and a liberal amount of survival maps which test the limit of the player's skill while in a team based setting; the game is first and foremost a co-op based survival shooter, not a Rambo style killing spree sort of game. The game leaves little to no room for mistakes for the player in the sense that you only have a limited amount of resources such as ammunition and, most importantly, medkits and vital pills for treating the viral infection that turns you into a zombie and which must be wisely distributed amongst team members which even then, won't be enough for everyone to go around. Another aspect worth mentioning would have to be the difficulty implanted within the game, it's pretty hard to begin with and you can't change the difficulty level leaving you with an ever-increasing sense of agony and fear when you're faced with mindless flesh eating zombies advancing towards you with little to no room for fleeing -- a scenario you'll definitely run into throughout the game! Anyway, I strongly encourage all of my peers to try this one out -- you won't regret it!!!!

okay here is my review for dmc: devil may cry
first of all, this is a reboot so if there is anyone who is hating the storyline because it's not the same as the other 4. bye.
So this game came out on sale and me being the smart minded Steam shopper it was only normal to buy the game without looking at reviews and videos, and I'm glad I bought it because this game is really fun. Long story short (with no spoilers ofc) this game starts off as you playing as Dante awakening up from another night of being hungover and partying. You hear someone knocking on your door and it's just a random girl telling you you're in danger, demon comes out of nowhere smashes the trailer Dante was living in, puts you in limbo and screams dying pterodactyl noises. Fast forward boss fight and goose chasing, random girl takes you on a car ride to introduce you to a person named Vergil. He explains to you about the demon king Mundus and how he has a grip on the entire planet, reveals your past and basically described that Dante is a Nephilim (half angel/demon) and must help defeat demon king for only a nephilim can stand up to someone such as Mundus. And this is pretty much the shortest summary I could write without giving too much of the story, but just because the summary is short doesn't mean the story is. The story can go deeper than just a bunch of angels and demons fighting.
Before I actually talk about gameplay I can't give any personal opinion on how the keyboard and mouse controls are because during the time I played this game I had no wifi and only an Xbox One controller to help play through this and everything worked and responded perfectly. So if you want to do some offline gaming this game should give almost no problems.
So as for gameplay, I can tell you the combat system for the majority of Dante's weapons are all unique and serve as a goal or advantage for you in the game. Such as fighting particular demons or using it to break something down. The way the combos are mapped out are hard to get used to at first because as the story progresses you can just keep getting new weapons and you're just telling yourself what the hell, because you're still trying to master your previous weapons and there's just really so much combos to do with any weapon it's ridiculous. To actually get new combos you have to continue fighting demons because they drop red and white orbs so this will act as currency and you can use these to upgrade either your health, or increase Dante's handling of all his weapoons.
It's really hard to feel a sense of "wow i beat these guys already this is too repetitive" because like I said there are particular demons that can only be beaten with particular weapons so if you start getting that feeling then try a different approach in handling the enemy. If combos aren't refreshing your experience with different mobs then definitely the music will help. As someone who enjoys metal and as for anyone who enjoys the genre the game has so much, you just feel so into the game when you're introduced to something new because the music in-game is just so amazing you can't help but get sucked into the combat and start going crazy.  Another thing about the game is that there is no regenerative health system so you have to play your cards right in how you go about fighting because some demons could be just as damaging as you and they're gonna come at you at all angles, because of this you can get a sense of fear. Fear from getting hit too much rather than fear from seeing their faces, although some faces really are horrifying but that's just my opinion.
So all in all this game can get pretty deep with gameplay, story can get pretty deep too but it's not mind exploding or boggling. In terms of length you're gonna get it's gonna get AT LEAST 15-20 hours on your first playthrough. The game has multiple difficulties though but those are unlocked if you beat the previous difficulty and if you do try out the harder difficulties the game rewards you with artwork and achievements. And there is A LOT of art to be showed, like previous art designs, sword art (get it) enemy art, etc.
Would I recommend this game? absolutely, does this game completely♥♥♥♥♥♥the previous storylines, no idea. This is my first dmc game and it was a really enjoyable experience that everyone should try out, but get this on sale because 50 dollars for this game is not exactly the price of what you're getting.

While I am choosing to not recommend this game, I'd rather this review be seen as a "Meh" or "Average." DmC hits many things really well, and then falls flat on its face in others. I would like to preface by saying that I haven't played the original DMC games, but I have played Hideki Kamiya's Bayonetta, so my comparison will be based a bit around that.
By now, it should be well known that this reboot's Dante is a black haired, foul mouthed early twenty-or-something troublemaker. While a big problem is how he compares to the original Dante, for this review I'll mostly be looking at the reboot as its own series separate from Kamiya's. So how does this Dante hold up as his own character? He's not necessarily a bad character. He displays growth, and becomes less bull headed and more concerned for others such as Kat. Some of his lines and actions are actually really good too, with his attitude being a perfect contrast for some of the serious guys there such as Vergil (in one particular scene, he answers Vergil with a shrug and "So what?" when Vergil brings up the idea of freeing the citizens). Dante exemplifies the punk movement, which is what he (and to an extent the society around him) was based off of, and I think he does a good job with it.
That isn't to say he's the
character ever written, but he was the best in this game, as all the other character become really boring and flat to follow. Vergil is written awkwardly, with a shallow emotional spectrum to accompany him; essentially, he is our exposition machine. Kat is so flat I don't even know what she was doing in there. She does something action wise, but personality wise I can barely remember what her personality was after finishing the game 10 minutes ago - it's
. Mundus and his minions are all stereotypical demonic villains, looking to rule the world. Nothing about the writing sticks out, and many attempts at banter or funny one liners fail and just sound awkward. The voice acting for Dante is the best most of the time, but there are still a few parts when his voice actor seems to be new and they didn't go for a second take.
The game does shine when it comes to its art direction, its music, and its combat system. The art, with the contrasts for Limbo and the original city, are great to see, and the music was cool to listen to as I'm slashing away at demons. One thing to note is that, if you don't like punk, or growling vocals, then this soundtrack will not be for you. The combat itself is apparently dumbed down, from what I hear, but it's not a bad thing for new players. I personally don't play much hack-n-slash so this was a good thing for me, I think, but I can see some veterans becoming bored (in which case I recommend playing the hardest difficulties). When I played I never got anything below an A, on medium, so maybe this can indicate how difficult the game is. It was still very satisfying combat, especially when it came to the harder to kill enemies, and getting those combos were awesome.
However, I did find that there seemed to be a delay between inputting button commands, as many times I went to strike and wanted to dodge an incoming enemy attack, but I had to wait at least half a second to a second for my input to actually register as dodge. This can be annoying and especially frustrating on harder enemies. Furthermore, this game has a lot of platforming, more than I expected, which can be annoying at times; it also has a lot of cutscenes, sometimes with only a tiny element of gameplay (moving Dante to the next point) involved, which can be annoying as well if you want to get straight into the action. There's also no lock-on button, which can be absolutely bothersome combined with a frozen camera (see below).
Some minor gripes: I played on a controller, and often times the camera would lock up and prevent me from spinning it, resulting in me getting hit by enemies. I'm not sure if playing with a KB+M is better, but I heard it is decent. Also, in comparing to the original DMC games, I wish this Dante would flourish his weapons each time he got them, but alas, Ninja Theory did not do that.
Overall, DmC is certainly not a bad game gameplay and art wise, but the story is horrid. I recommend purchasing it on sale, and only if you're interested in the combat. If you like story based games, this one is not written well and will possibly disappoint you.

If you need convincing though, let’s talk about the talking points people care about.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
[Episodic Gaming Done Right]
The game wasn’t and still isn’t like the early access trash you see around today. All the game mechanics are polished and functioning how a triple A title should.  The game is complete, they just staggered the release of the levels in the game. This was actually a perfect decision in terms of gameplay because it promotes the player to replay the older levels again, which is probably one of the most rewarding parts of the game. You unlock more freedom and options in each level the more you play that level, giving access to disguises, weapons, starting points, etc. which will help you create those perfect assassinations you are trying to create.
Anyone complaining about the episodic nature of this game have no ♥♥♥♥ing idea what they are talking about. If a Season 2 is made, I hope more consumers have found some more brain cells.
Edit: You can now only buy it as a complete set, but you can play the tutorial missions as a demo if you still are not convinced
[Elusive Targets]
They take an already established level, change a few things up and create a new target to kill. The catch is that the mission is only available for a limited time, you cannot save, and you only have one shot to complete it. What this means is if you get killed you cannot do the mission again. You can restart the mission again and again to scope out the environment and plan your attack. But, once you actually kill the target you cannot restart and must escape or you lose. People complain that these mission should always be available, those people are wrong. They changes to the levels are so minor that the mission can resemble created contracts that are made by the community, the only thing that really makes these missions fun and intense is the fact that you only have one shot. I personally have failed probably 5 or so the assassination, and straight up missed maybe 8 of them. I'm bumded out I lost, but I dont feel like I was cheated out of content.
[Always Online]
Originally there was an issue that if you played offline the game would not give you any of your unlockables or your story progression. This is NO LONGER the case, you can now play offline with all your items. People complaining about always online literally have nothing to cry about anymore, yet the idiots still do.
[Conclusion]
It’s one of the best Triple A games to come out in the last 10 years. You may not get the same experience as me now that you can play it all at once, but the amount of content they continue to add monthly even after the game was “finished” is something to be applauded. Recently they added a hard mode which basically is Ocarina of Time’s Master Quest. All levels have been changed to increase difficulty (moved/removed items, added cameras, etc.), now only having one time to save per mission, an AI Buff, and gameplay mechanic additions (can ruin disguises / suspicion via held item). If you are thinking about picking this game up do so, it is well worth its asking price. And if you aren’t convinced, try the demo.
If you are a Hitman/Stealth fan you won’t be disappointed.

Russian, WWII-era Hitman.  I didn't really even know anyone had ever attempted to do something like Hitman. And what a brilliant mix, a Hitman game about killing Nazis!
Okay, so first off, this game ran fine (Windows 7 x64 still), in widescreen at good resolution without any effort on my part whatsoever, all I had to do was disable depth of field to get rid of some nasty textures.  You can't even get most Hitman games to run in widescreen without doing all sorta funky hacks, and again, its a Russian game, most Russian games I've played required serious effort to get running on any modern system.
That outta the way. HOW DID I MISS THIS!?! I love the Hitman games, and this is arguably better than some of the old Hitmans, maybe even on par with Blood Money (maybe, I reserve judgement until I've finished the game).  I've never heard of Death to Spies until this sale, which really sucks because it does some things better than even Hitman does. For starters, if you shoot a dude anywhere but in the head, or if you slit his throat//stab him, the uniform he's wearing has bulletholes/blood stains, which are a dead-giveaway, so you can't use it.  Small, simple, brilliant. The objectives are a lot different, the primary focus isn't necessarily assassination like it is in Hitman, you're more of a spy than an assassin in many cases, you just have a license to kill and you USE IT =D
Second, this game rates your performance waaaayyyy differently, killing someone other than your designated target doesn't automatically bone you out of the highest ratings, its more about how professional, silent and clean you are. Strangle a guard and hide the body - and containers to put bodies in are rare in this game, you just have to dump them somewhere out of the way - and you're golden; make a mess, have a body get found, or set off an alarm though and your score is obviously penalized like most stealth games.  If they find a naked body you've taken the uniform for, they start looking for intruders wearing that uniform, making it useless and lowering your score.  However, you have a backpack, and you can actually carry disguises with you, again something we've never seen from Hitman. You have to do more than wear the clothes though, if you're disguised as a Nazi soldier, you need to swap out Russian weaponry for German weaponry, found on bodies usually, or you can choose to start the mission with German guns in most/all cases. If they see you using Russian guns while posing as a German sentry, their suspicion of you raises very quickly. Additionally, your dude can go prone and crawl, which is really useful in open, outdoor sections without generous cover (not to mention making sniping a hell of a lot easier).
You do have a non-lethal option, namely a bottle of chloroform that works similar to how it did in Hitman 2 though it has 5-10 uses and 1 use knocks out an enemy for the rest of the mission, whereas knockouts in H2 only lasted minutes. You can also just punch someone in the face, but its not as effective and is noisy. Also of note, you can actually drive vehicles in this game, which was never a thing in Hitman; its useful too since the maps are pretty big; you can even use a truck that has a canopy to hide a body and move it around. On the hardest difficulty, the ability to take disguises is removed entirely, which basically equates to some missions being impossible to get through without garroting a few patrols and guards, however you also get an automatic score boost, to rectify any loose ends you had to tie up.
I'm excited for the third one, it originally failed a kickstarter I think, and its not the original developers or publishers, and its more of a spiritual successor than direct sequel since its a different main character and set in the Cold War, but they have something here, excited to see where they go with it ---

I'm going to start this review with on statement that I believe to be true.
Death to Spies is essentially a carbon copy of Hitman in a WW2 setting. A lot of the gameplay will be extremely familiar to you and you will enjoy it the same way you enjoyed Hitman. Hell, it's even got an "A new life" type of level where there's a house being guarded by the feds, and the game plays out like Hitman: Contracts, where you watch as Agnet 47 wakes up and then play through his memories of the missions that led up to this point.
Death to Spies has all of that.
If you haven't played Hitman, but you're interested in Death to Spies, the game basically works as a giant playground of strategic freedom. You enter the level, receive your objectives, and then the game stops holding your hand while you work out everything yourself. You choose what order you'll complete the objectives in, how many people you'll kill, and plant all kinds of traps to catch your enemy off guard.
My main problems with this game is that the controls can be a little clunky at times, and that CTRL+S quicksaves, for some reason. F5 already does that, game. I don't need another control to do that for me.
Other than that, Death to Spies: Moment of Truth, is an exciting extension of Hitman that I would definitely recommend to any stealth strategy fans.

When you and your teammates have set up a base everyone can go to for health and ammo you feel like you're the best and most cooperative players ever. And everyone helps too! In other games people are huge jerks, and especially from a FREE game like this you'd expect stupid behavior, but it's really not that bad. Which surprised me.
Also, zombies. Finally the zombies are done right, slow and bullet-eating. The only edge they have on you is the fact that you don't have munition and they have fists. A lot of them. They are hard to take down, so when they start blocking both paths, you're screwed. Even though they're practically standing still. The other thing they can do is bite and infect you, and when you're bit you better hope there's pills nearby, because you're gonna turn into a zombie soon. And you'll be a fast zombie too, posing a real threath to your team. The best thing you can do when you're beyond saving is running into the horde with a shotgun and dying a hero's death. That way, maybe your team can and survive so you can respawn after the wave. If you turn into a zombie behind the firing line however, your team will be attacked from behind which can mean the end of your team, so don't do that.
A zombie game like this, where the focus is more on gathering supplies than combat (i.e. CoD zombies), is something I've been looking for, and here it is. Completely free. I don't even have to convince you, it's free, you have nothing to lose! Sadly, the devs have nothing to win either (which they absolutely deserve), but at least check this out, it's what they would have wanted.

Mahjong World Contest is a solitaire mahjong game (and saying that will earn me some comments that solitaire mahjong doesn't exist). Anyway, the goal is to clear a level by matching tiles with the same number/pattern. Here, you have three objectives if you want to score 3 stars in a level. However, the most important objective to unlock the next level is to remove every gold tile. Other objectives are usually scoring points and moves.
You have six "rooms", unlocked only when you're reaching a new title (thanks to scoring stars). However, it's not really representative of an increase in difficulty: I've managed to clear easily many of them in one or two tries. However, two or three of them made me nuts as I was always above the maximum moves allowed for the star. Despite trying to know by heart the gold tiles locations, it was really hard.
You don't have many helps apart hightlighting what can be removed and a shuffle option if you're stuck (if no moves, it will trigger automatically) - in other words, if you don't find tiles matching or if you're judging that you will make more moves that necessary. Shuffling allows you to match more tiles.
The graphics are just average: nothing really fancy but still nice. The soundtrack is also relaxing.
As much as I would like to expand the review, there is nothing really to say: it's just plain mahjong, without plot, without bonus or special tiles (like in good old Mahjong Quest), no other modes, nothing. It will satisfy mahjong players but will bore after a while many other players as nothing is really breaking the rhythym.
Should I recommend it? Mahjong World Contest is one of these games where a neutral rating would be nice as yes, I can recommend it for fans but no, because the price is a little too high for what it is. Going to put a positive rating but I'm really aware that it could have been a negative rating if I didn't enjoy the challenge.

It's your standard Mahjong game, though it lacks any particular innovation whilst the lack of a widescreen option is ridiculous for a game released in 2016. If you are okay with those points my only suggestion is to maybe avoid the "shuffle" button as pressing it has caused the game to crash to the point that not even the task manager can be brought up to attempt to force close the program; I trust this may be fixed in the future.

I want to start off by saying that I completely understand why fans of the old Devil May Cry franchise don't like this game. And let me follow that up with reminding people that this is a WESTERN RE-IMAGINING OF A JAPANESE GAME, thus things will change including character motivations and designs.
If you look at this game as EXACTLY what it is (Re-imagining) and NOT what people want it to be (apples-to-apples remake and/or sequel/prequel), you will find that while it does have it's faults, it's still a good game. Gameplay while easier than the original, is much more fast-paced and still presents it's share of challenges. Story admittedly isn't terribly deep, but I kind of found the idea of the world interesting and while the satire of American cultural ideas is anything but subtle, it is satisfying to play with the idea that some of the things wrong with the country are headed by demonic powers and thus correct them in an over-the-top way.
Lastly, I want to say that with some of the things people seemed to have lost their mind over (namely a very short cutscene in the first level), I want to say to them FINISH THE GAME. Dante changes throughout the game, growing as most young people do. In the end, I could sum up almost all complaints about this game as being a over-blown case of "Judging a Book by it's Cover". Do I reccomend this game to new fans of the franchise? Yes. Do I reccomend it to old fans of the franchise? Yes, if you're willing to see what this game is, rather than what it isn't.

I started playing Hitman games relatively late, my first was Blood Money which has remained the gold standard for the series. Absolution, while a good game in its own right was a mediocre (at best) Hitman game, but this....this new installment is utterly fantastic.
Bringing over Instinct and the Contracts mode from Absolution (and significantly improving them) while going back to the more open-ended style of Blood Money and the earlier games, combined with an excellent attention to detail and finely crafted levels; IO Interactive has produced a game which absolutely ticks all my boxes.
While it may seem that there's not much content with only 6 main missions, each mission can be tackled and completed in dozens of different ways. Each mission also has a set of challenges which you can complete to gain mastery and unlock new weapons and gear to use. Add on to that the 3 bonus missions which take place in reworked (sometimes substantially so) versions of some of the main missions and all of the Escalations, and there is an unexpectedly large amount of content to explore.
The game is brilliantly conceived and very fun to play.  Pre-alpha means bugs and crashes, of which there are many.  I'm excited to see how this game grows over time.

HITMAN™ is a game that's really hard to like. There's a lot to do overall; I'm 35 hours in and I'm barely scratching the surface. There is tons of challenges and feats which you can attempt for additional playtime. And then there's bonus episode and elusive targets. However, there's a lot of game mechanics that's frustrating. For example, sometimes NPC will spot you/hidden bodies from across the map through 3 sets of concrete walls with their x-ray visions ( a liitle exageration, but you get the picture). But since you can save/load at nearly all the time, if something does come up you can usually make a few changes and everything will resume normal.
There are two things that may or may not be a deciding factor for you though. The story of HITMAN™ is not complete. It basically ends with a cliff hanger with the conclusion of season one. And although, at some point, there will be a release of season 2 for HITMAN™. Nothing is set in stone yet. If not being able to get the complete story troubles you, you might want to wait until the dust settles and the whole story pans out before getting into it.
Another thing to take into consideration is the DRM. Although I haven't personally experience this issue. Apparently, you need a constant connection to enjoy challenges and whatnot. So if a stable connection is an issue for you I'd suggest you play something else.
To reiterate, HITMAN™ is a good game. But corporate greed weighs on this title, thus limiting it's potential. Had the games not come with online DRM. Or under threat of getting scrapped, I would absolutely recommend this to any hitman/open world fan.
(P.S: As of this writing, I would also like to mention that this game suffers terrible obtimization. In terms of graphics. I found myself staring at a jagged circle and blurry sign at times.)

It's good to see the franchise back in good shape, after coldly (and for good reasons) received Absolution.
- big maps
- many (if not too many) ways to approach objectives
- excellent visuals and audio
- decent AI
I had a blast playing the game, and it would be hypocritical to not recommend it, but - nothing is perfect, and from my subjective point of view, there're obvious and not so obvious flaws that need to be pointed out:
- hard difficulty mode - added at least a year too late and HIDDEN behind extensive "map mastery" GRIND. It's so idiotic I don't even know what to say. Every Hitman (even Absolution) lets you select difficulty mode from the start. But nooo, not this one. Let's FORCE people to replay maps multiple times to collect stupid opportunities before they're generously allowed to choose harder difficulty. This also implies opening walkthrough on the second monitor or neutering difficulty by enabling instincts and handholding misfeatures; and then just grrrrrind that mastery level up to 20.
♥♥♥♥ you, whoever though that would be good idea. You should be fired and not allowed by law to ever touch this franchise or any other stealth game. Perhaps you played too many brainless korean mmos ?
- escalations - or - how to - halfassedly - attempt to make the maps suffice longer, which brings us to:
- episodic approach; this wasn't much of an issue for me as I got the game when it was finished (and as such I could enjoy the whole game as it should be - 6 main missions + few smaller ones) - but for people that played it "episodically" - I feel bad for them; I hope they enjoyed escalations fillers =) Though the same fate awaits for me with season 2 (if it's coming at all)
- de-facto online only mode/DRM, regressing the game to a basic state when there're issues with online connection (regardless of the reasons - "yours" or "theirs"); note that the "online" element is deeply sew into the game - some of this stuff somehow understandable (elusive targets) some other not so much (escalations, scores, unlocks, challenges, mission preparation, saves, etc.); and this might be an issue a few years from now - as it's notably more than just DRM and will require extensive patching to remove/replace it
- online-only addendum: the game will kick you out if you lose connection (thought it will give you an option to retry - so you have a chance to fix the issues if they are on your side)
- instinct nonsense from Absolution is sadly back, along with other handholding misfeatures; thankfully they can all be turned off - so this is not a big deal; seriously though, the time could be spent on some other elements of the game
Anyway, good things outweight bad ones by far. If you like stealth, get the game and enjoy some quality 47 gameplay.

Rust is unique among survival games in that it provides an unknown need for social interaction. Rust by itself understands the need for human interaction. Ever tried running a solo server? The game needs optomizations like most games, but it is nice to see a game that has handled its ups and downs. There are a lot of times where people hated a new system in the game, such as crafting, yet after a while everyone overcomes and adapts simply because you cannot move forwards if you try to move backwards. Spec Ops: The Line is probably the hardest game to play. Not so much because of its difficulty but because the theme it presents, the settings.
You take control of a 3 man team, capt. Walker, Lugo and Adams are sent into the deep end of Dubai, tasked to find the 33 squad. But the more they go further, the more they realise that the once luxurious city became a living hell, where its every man for himself. There are no heroes,  there are are no good or bad choices you need to make: but to sometimes having to decide between the lesser evil.
While many games nowadays tries to dehumanise war, this one pulls no string to show you the consequences of your actions, without trying to do any sort of guilt- tripping.   Even more depressing to think that while this may be just a game, in many countries this is an everyday reality.........
The game  breaks the fourth wall at many occasions and among other things  asks one simple question to the player: "Do you feel like a hero yet?", which never felt as gutt-wrenching and tear-jerking as it did in this game.

I wish there was a way to provide a number rating rather than a simple yes or no.  Arkham Origins is definitely the weakest of the 3 Arkham games that I have played.  On the one hand, you could say that if you play them in order (Origins, Asylum, then City) that it would get progressively better to the point of getting a bat boner...and that's fine.  Origins suffers from just plain bad design.
The map is too large.  It's large for the sake of being large.  With the other Arkham games, the maps were large, but they were chock full of interesting content.  This was an obvious cash-in title, so while there are things that I like, the game focuses way too much on collectibles to the point I thought this was Banjo-Kazooie.  Riddler trophies range from stupidly simple to annoying.
At least in Arkham City even the easy trophies required a bit of puzzle elements to navigate through.  Most of the easy trophies in this game involve randomly tripping over them or shocking something, then just pick it up or whatever.  But by far the worst part of this game, and I'm going to try to be as spoiler free as possible, is the final villain.  Such an obvious choice after presenting so many different characters that only the most diehard Batman fans will know about (Firefly, Deathstroke, Shiva, Black Mask, Electrocutioner, etc.).
And the events leading up to the final fight?  What, a brute fight with advanced enemies, an advanced enemy mob fight, a repeat of the Mr. Freeze fight from Arkham City but not as good, then a couple of counters and a stupid beatdown sequence.  It wasn't bad enough that the game had a higher encounter rate than older Final Fantasy titles or that it was obviously trying desperately to be Arkham City and falling WAY short, then they completely screw up the final act like that.
I won't say to save your money.  It's still part of the Arkham series and is actually fun.  Just keep in mind that it's a very weak entry.  I'm still looking forward to Arkham Knight and even the 2.5D Blackgate game, but I've heard they also aren't that great.  If you don't own Arkham Asylum and City, get those instead.  If you own them already and you're REALLY desperate for more content AND this game is on sale...yeah, okay, then I would get it.

This is a distinctly beautiful game, and, as others have said, achieves near perfection. The game knows exactly what it wants to be, and manages it pretty much flawlessly. The visual art, the stroy, the animations, the music, the controlls, the levels, all are absolutely stellar. The beginning will make you sniffle and bring a lump to your throat, and the end will make you straight-up cry (or at least it did for me). This is a game about beauty, and the triumph of goodness and love over hate and bitterness. It's also a surprisingly punishing game in its combat and platforming, and distinctly rewarding. There are several escape sections in particular (which serve as Ori's boss fights) that are absolutely brutal, but leave you with immense satisfaction when finished. The difficulty never feels unfair. The progession of upgrades, both choosen and bestowed, feels well balanced and steadily unlocked powers that expand the traversable world.
Overall, Ori is simply a wonderful game and a beautiful experience. You won't get hundreds of hours out of this game (with 97% completion, I've put about 15 hours into the game), but the hours you do put in are so well spent. Buy this game. It's not very expensive on sale, and totally worth it.

Overall would highly recommend-- even if you're not a fan of the genre.

I am a huge fan of the Hitman series (with Blood Money topping my personal charts) and had this game on my whislist for quite some time but never got around to getting it. One day it came on sale and I thought "why not? time to get it".
Now I regret not making this decision earlier.
If you are a Hitman fan YOU MUST PLAY THIS GAME. It may not have the same level of polish and production values but it more than makes up for with amazing level design and a solid sneaking and disguising mechanic. In that respect it's actually better than Hitman.
It's much easier in this game to understand what your enemies are up to, who is detecting you and why. This eliminates almost entirely those situations that occured in Hitman where your cover would be blown for no apparent reason. It's not very realistic but it fits the gameplay really well. And you can always play on highest difficulty with no helpers. Still, even with the helpers, the game is difficult enough and very punishing if you don't take your time. This is not for people who lack patience.
My only dissapointment is that there are only 7 missions. Then again, they are extremely intricate and each one took me at least an hour to complete on my first playthrough (with some taking over two hours).
One other negative which personally doesn't bother me because it's not how I play this game is concerning shooting mechanics. They are bad. I mean really bad. They're good enough to get you out of a tight situation (a silenced Nagant is a dirty but effective way of disposing of a nozy nazi) but don't think you can shoot your way through missions.
Overall though this is a great game and I'm eager to see what's next when DtS 3 comes out.

Firstly, this game is quite impressive from an indy developer. The visuals, sound, voice overs and music are equal to what huge triple-A developers are making these days. Graphics are insane. When you're in the woods, it actually really sounds and feels like you're in actual woods. Then why rate this game with a thumbs down, might you ask? It's pacing and story.
This game has a pretty simple story for most of the game, there's something that happened and you slowly unravel people's lives around the event. However the story got real wacky at the end and it just didn't feel right. The game went from a really chill and simple story when a lot of relatable backstory on people's lives involving friends, family, relationships. Then the ending comes along and s*** gets wack.
That's obviously an issue itself, but I found pacing to be a huge issue too. There isn't much to do in this game besides walking around to the next area to hear audio clips of a slowly progressing story via clicking on things, or just entering certain areas. This game is a walking sim, big time. Pacing is an issue in the story because it just grows so slowly without introducing an interesting amount of new content or characters. This is a very, very beautiful walking sim but the scenery, however very incredible, does get a bit old since there really isn't much to do other than look at stuff.
I wish there were a lot of hidden trinkets in some places that you could collect--just somehting to do other than look around for the next area to get closer to the ending. Interactivity is extremely limited and it would help the game hugly if there were more things to touch and play around with or find.
Voice overs are done quite well. The English accents are nice, espically in my American ears. However what they talk about half the time is a bit boring. Not all conversations you hear help progress the story. There is a lot of filler, voice over wise.
Movement is weird. You are forced to walk real slow most of the time. There is a run function when you press shift, but the game doesn't let you use it most of the time. And when it does, you have to hold down shift for a good 5 sec plus just to speed up a little bit. Lastly, when you can "run" it's just a slightly faster walk. I imagine they did this to either pad the runtime, or force you to appreciate the visuals, or both.
This game also is a semi-open world game. There are open areas you can explore, like little towns and stuff, of which some houses you can enter. These open areas are inbetween tight pathcs. There are even a few slightly open-world wooded areas, which are my fav. parts of the game as they feel so amazing. Vegetation is very impressive and seems to be a huge focus in this game, as far as showing off is concerned.
Anyways, the story needs to be reworked and tons of flavor needs to be added to it. Thicken and strenghten it up. You can't put such a mellow (for most of the game) and slow story in a walking sim. It needs some balls and something more to grab me and keep me interested, as I lost interest part-way through and just wanted to finish the game. I am quite certain people who are impatient will hate this game with a passion.

You either *click with* and enjoy such experiences, or move on and enrich your life with other preferred types of games.
It is very much in the vein of Chinese Room's previous game - "Dear Esther", but builds on every aspect of it and the end product is gorgeous and unforgettable. If you liked any of  "Dear Esther", "Gone Home", "Tacoma", "Firewatch", "The Vanishing of Ethan Carter" (though the last two contain more game mechanics) - you'll like EGTTR too. Conversely, if you're alergic to "walking sims" - stay away from this, It ranks among the best of THEM.

Batman: Arkham origins is a brilliant game if you're a fan of the previous arkham games. The plot follows Bruce's earlier days in the dawn of the bat where he deals with the lack of trust from the police and in turn: Commissioner Gorden.
This extra wave of enemies adds a bit of variety of people you're beating up differentiating from the usual thugs and criminals. I personally like the story and missions classing in a half stealth, half action genre as you battle against the different villians from Gotham, some more recognisable than others dependant on your knowledge of the universe.
Gameplay
===================================================================
Featuring the same combat system as the previous games, it is as satisfying as ever! However, if you've grown tired of it by now it might be a good idea to wait for a bit and come back to this. The unlockable gadgets are pretty good: things such as the different batarangs returning with new iterations in the form of shock gloves (A bit OP but fun :3) and glue grenades. While the main story is great to complete, the amount of side content is huge! Ranging from crime scene investigations to helping to track down runaway criminals. The game also features an online mode which, while fun, is quite hard to consistantly play with long loading/ lobby times and a not so active community. If you can bear the waiting the actual multiplayer is very fun both on hero and villian sides.
===================================================================
Story, characters, bosses ect.
===================================================================
The story is a good one as Batman finds out about the Joker himself, battling unique assassins on the side (my favourite being deathstroke) These assassins serve as the bosses in the game and each are interesting and different even with some taking inspiration from the previous games. As for Batman, you get to see how hard it is for him being a hero and protecting the people he's close to such as Alfred, I wish Robin was in this other than the multiplayer though ;-;
===================================================================
Final pros, cons
===================================================================
Pros-
-Fluent and fun combat system
-Hell of a lot of content
-Decent story
-Uses lesser known awesome villians
-Fun stealth elements
Cons-
-Annoying online
-Can be repetative
-Similar to previous games
Final verdict- 8/10, Would recommend: If the multiplayer was more active with more maps and a bit of variation was put into some of the missions i'd probably give it a 10.

I finished Max Payne 2 directly after finishing the first game. I recommended that and the same apply's here.
In terms of change between the two games, I didn't really feel there was much. Bullet time is less about jumping while trying to shoot as many enemys as possible and more about triggering before entering a room and trying to clear the room before the bullet time's over. I have to admit I didn't really like the change, while fun in itself I always liked the more carefully planned approach of the original. The difficulty in general after how careful you had to be in the original was just a minor annoyance on what is otherwise a fantastic sequal.
This game stands the test of time nicely. You won't find it ugly or out of place with modern day games. The sound comes together just how you'd want it to, the game still contains that wonderful Max Payne theme.
It ran well on my fairly modern system (Windows 8 64bit, 1920x1080 resolution etc) You shouldn't have any problems here although there has been known to be issues with other players. (Check the forums first)
I would have to finish by saying both Max Payne and Max Payne 2 are very similar, both are short experiences, both have fun, solid and replayable gameplay, wonderful soundtracks and great storys. I would fully recommend at the cheap price it sells at today.

A challenging, but fun platformer. Super Meat Boy delivers a good experience.
Graphics: The graphics are well-made, it looks like they intended it to be a flash game from the beginning if you ask me. I rate the graphics 9/10.
Gameplay: The gameplay is great, good old platforming. Beware though, the game is
. It's not just a little bit hard, the difficulty is near games released for the NES if you know what i mean. Don't be suprised if you fail a level multiple times, you'll pass it eventually. However, to compensate for the high difficulty, you have unlimited lives, so you don't have to worry about getting a game over. You can also find bandages on some levels which, if you collect enough, you will unlock a new character to play as. However, i do recommend to use a controller to play the game, as the keyboard controls can be a bit akward. Overall, the gameplay is great. 10/10.
Story: The story is very video game-clichê like, you have the main character, Meat Boy, who has a girlfriend, Bandage Girl. They love each other. The villain is Dr. Fetus, a guy nobody likes. One day, out of anger, he kidnaps Bandage Girl, and Meat Boy must rescue her. As you can see, the plot is
similiar to any Super Mario game. I give the story 6/10.
Music: The music is fantastic, it gets you warmed-up for some hard platforming action. Every theme fits perfectly where they are played. 10/10.
In conclusion, Super Meat Boy is a challenging, but rewarding and fun game. However, not everyone will appreciate the high difficulty the game has. If you don't like dying over and over, the game might not be for you. However, if you're a hardcore gamer who wants a good challenge, then pick this game up. You won't regret it.
Final Score: 8/10.

This game is awesome and has ridiculous potential. In its pre-alpha state it has the feel of a condensed version of no man's sky (if it were done right). initially the player begins with a simple "habitat" that they can enter to protect themselves from violent random weather events that fling debris to and fro (getting hit by the debris instantly kills the player).
The player must seek out raw materials surrounding the landing craft at a limited range, due to the small oxygen capacity of the astronaut's suit, which can be replenished by standing at a close proximity to the craft. Once the player has enough materials to build basic necessities (such as "tethers" which are placed on the ground to extend the oxygen refill range of the landing craft), the real adventure begins.
In order to build the more advanced items, the player must find rare materials that can only be located in random "crash sites" on the surface, or deep within treacherous caves with many pitfalls, traps, and dangerous flora. By researching objects in the world, more buildable items become available for the player to add to their primary base of operation.
Once a player's base is fully built and upgraded, they may choose to build a landing craft or a spaceship to shoot into orbit. Doing so will allow the player to land on other far-away locations on their home planet if they want to explore, or to travel to other planets nearby. My home planet had a moon, bountiful with rare materials on and under its surface.
This game was a great experience, although there were a few bugs that were slightly annoying:
when sliding down an inclined surface, the character would often get stuck in "slide mode" even after the slope ended, resulting in what looks like an astronaught on skates. Jumping will cancel this effect.
When landing a spaceship on another planet, the player has the option to extend platforms from its base (not really sure what it's for yet, as the only thing the player can make from them are more platforms). doing so will make a "tube" connecting the platform and the spaceship, and when the player decides to take off, the spaceship takes the tube with it and makes it "stretch" infinitely. even when landing on other planets, the player will see a tube stretching off into space, presumably still trying to attach to the platform made on the initial planet. So far I haven't found any way to detach the spaceship from the platform.
Upon death, the player keeps whatever they were holding in their hands when they respawn, and also respawns with solar panels still attached if they made solar panels.
sometimes tethers seem to randomly disconnect from other tethers, making a break in the line. This can be fixed by picking them up and placing them in the same spot usually.
If the player is too close to a building site when they construct a new module for their base, they will get stuck inside the foundation of the structure with no way to escape other than quitting the game and reloading it.
Vehicles tend to get stuck on EVERYTHING and have difficulting dealing with inclines. if they get flipped over press tab to flip them back. Also, connecting a trailer to a vehicle caused it to drive weird.

I started playing Hitman games relatively late, my first was Blood Money which has remained the gold standard for the series. Absolution, while a good game in its own right was a mediocre (at best) Hitman game, but this....this new installment is utterly fantastic.
Bringing over Instinct and the Contracts mode from Absolution (and significantly improving them) while going back to the more open-ended style of Blood Money and the earlier games, combined with an excellent attention to detail and finely crafted levels; IO Interactive has produced a game which absolutely ticks all my boxes.
While it may seem that there's not much content with only 6 main missions, each mission can be tackled and completed in dozens of different ways. Each mission also has a set of challenges which you can complete to gain mastery and unlock new weapons and gear to use. Add on to that the 3 bonus missions which take place in reworked (sometimes substantially so) versions of some of the main missions and all of the Escalations, and there is an unexpectedly large amount of content to explore.

It's the better version of No MAn's sky for a really reasonable price.
It has some bugs obviously since it's an early access game but nothing that makes the game unplayable.
Graphics are awesome and building in this game is a lot of fun.
Give it a try, you won't regret it.

HITMAN is a return to the style of Blood Money, not Absolution. That is, it is no longer a game which rams you into small levels and forced situations in the name of plot, and is instead satisfied with being a series of lavish, sprawling murder playgrounds stitched together with an easily-ignored plot. And god DAMN is this GREAT.
While the episodic format isn't necessarily how I'd like a game to be released, every one of the six episodes is a gem in the Blood Money tradition. These levels are large, complex, gorgeously-detailed areas which you can exploit in thousands of different ways. I think every level stands in its own way at, and usually above, the standards set by Blood Money.
Take Sapienza, an absolutely beautiful Italian coastal town. There's a church, gardens, tourists wandering through restaurants and shops, and a huge, lavish mansion with a chemical weapons lab in the basement. The game gives you the objective (Kill two scientists and destroy a vial) and dumps you into the action. Maybe I'll play it conservative and just keep breaking into apartments until I find a guard's uniform, then do a standard infiltration of the guard patrols. Or I'll steal some reefers from the neighborhood hippie and just get the targets stoned enough to wander away from their bodyguards. Or I'll dress up like a cook, slip some bad tomato sauce into the target's favorite Bolognese sauce, and take advantage of his subsequent puking episode by following him into the bathroom and drowning him in the toilet. Or I'll play his psychiatrist and end the session with a Silverballer prescription. Or exploit his mommy issues by entrancing him with old family videos on a projector, and then interrupt his reverie by slashing his throat with a circumcision knife. Or dress up like a gardener and start Fargoing everybody in a mulcher. Or dress up like the other target's lover, lure her to a secret love nest, and bash her skull in with a golf club while she's enjoying a glass of wine. This is a madcap murder theme park par excellance.
And so replayable! Unlike Blood Money, this time certain actions earn you points, which unlock new items, weapons, and starting locations. Starting in a new location in a new costume, not to mention changing techniques in order to get more points, gives each level extensive replay value. The addition of a climbing mechanic opens up plenty of possibilities, allowing 47 to scuttle up and down buildings at will. The intuition system broadens your ability to calculate what you can and cannot do in any particular situation or disguise, while the combat seems have been beefed up to emphasize stealthy assassinations over gunfights. In addition, the points/achievement system forces you out of following a single kill pattern, challenging you to instead find different ways to dispose of the same target.
As far as gaming experiences go, this is a 10/10. It's a series of spectacular, open-ended homicide playgrounds stitched together by a plot which can be ignored completely if you wish, which was just what I was looking for.

HITMAN is a game developed by Io-Interactive and published by Sqaure Enix. HITMAN could be described as an “assassin sandbox” where you are free to kill the target in your own way
You play as Agent 47. He is a high skilled assassin, who works for the mysterious agency ICA
Most levels in this game work like this: you are set loose into an open world environment with people doing their jobs and things. Among those people there are your targets, that you have to kill. Observing patterns of movement is key: each NPC usually has a routine of places he/she goes and things he/she does
Agent 47 follows some kind of “perfect assassination honor code” where you are supposed to try to kill your targets in what is consedered the “perfect way”. So, there are some rules you should try to follow, such as: only kill the targets and no one eles, not being seen, destroying evidence and so on
Every time you violate one of these rules, you lose points, which reflects in losing potential unlockable stuff in the end of the mission
Everything is fine and dandy, so what went wrong?
Well, for starters, the abrupt announcment of an episodic model caught many off guard and turned a lot of people off. Many people, myself included, didn't want to get absorbed by the first level only to have to wait a month afterwards for the second, third, fourth, etc
We just waited for the game to be released fully. A game's release is the most important part of it's marketing blitz, so staggering that out over a year killed the hype for casual gamers eyeing the game at a glance
The end result was that I bought Season One during a sale. Having be thoroughly impressed, I was ready to buy Season Two, confident I would be getting my money's worth
Now it seems that Square Enix and Io-Interactive have parted ways, I'm honestly not so sure. I'm not sure if there'll even be a Season Two, and even if they contract another developer, it probably won't be the same
I'm worried that another team will never capture their same state of mind and design philosophy, assuming they even try at all
Square Enix made a very premature move by ridding themselves of Io-Interactive, and it's a shame that Io-Interactive no longer owns the franchise they've created...
HITMAN is a fun assassin sandbox and very fun to play, shame the shady business practices that Square Enix sought out and the stupid, dumb decisions Square Enix have made, may have ruined the Hitman franchise for good along with their other silly, dumb decisions that have cost fantastic series to go down the drain such as the Thief and Deus Ex franchises...

Hitman’s episodic first season draws to a close with the release of the Japan-set sixth episode, Situs Inversus.
Since March, players have been treated to a monthly instalment of Agent 47’s latest adventures. Shunning the usual distribution method, developers IO Interactive have split Hitman into a six episode season. The plot has taken the titular Hitman around the world, allowing us to visit exotic locations…and kill people.
We’ve sneaked around a Parisian fashion show, infiltrated a secret laboratory beneath a quaint Italian town, prevented a coup d’état in Marrakesh, added another rocker to the 27 club in Bangkok, taken on a redneck militia in Colorado and finished up in Hokkaido, Japan for the season finale.
Slipping back into the tailored suit of Agent 47 was a joy, this instalment offering refined gameplay across huge and varied locations. The patriarch of the stealth game, the Hitman franchise has always been about slipping in and taking out your target without detection.
The game requires planning and patience. Whilst a firefight is survivable, one man against an army of goons, or the local police force, isn’t very good odds. Luckily, Agent 47 is adept as the art of disguise and the use of make-shift weaponry.
Your first attempt at each mission gives you only the most basic of equipment and start location. Further play unlocks more options allowing you to customise your approach to your target.

The game’s huge detailed environments and the gap between episodes has afforded us the time to fully explore each location and partake in additional contracts created by both the community and ourselves. The developers own timed elusive targets, such as the memorable Wild Card mission whereby we had seven days to kill celeb target Gary Busey.
Six locations may not seem like much, but the game levels are immense and packed with routes, weapons and crowds of people just asking to be knocked out, have their clothes stolen as a disguise and their body hidden in a closet.
With challenges, and multiple assassination methods, Hitman offers immense replay value. Crafty poisonings, dodgy accidents or an old school bullet to the head via silenced pistol are just some of the way that Agent 47 dispatches his deserving and no-so-deserving victims.
The overarching plot that ties the assassinations together adds a Jason Bourne-style level of intrigue as it seems a shadowy organisation is using Agent 47’s abilities for their own agenda. The end of mission cut-scenes add this cinematic plot to an already technically adroit game.
The first season of this episodic Hitman game really delivers, offering interesting and diverse locations, complex and rewarding assassinations and the ability to create your own, or try someone else’s user-created missions. This, along with special escalations and time-limited elusive targets, makes Hitman a truly epic experience.
Verdict: 9/10

Attitude? Check. I love how badass and easygoing Dante is. No matter how ridiculously bad of a situation he's thrown into, the guy cannot be shaken. His whole personality is just amazing. Somewhere in the back of my mind, I think his character appeals to the same part of me that Spike Spiegel does from Cowboy Bebop, except Dante has more of a punk / rockstar vibe.
Style? Check. I really loved how so many elements to the game pushed this in-your-face, action movie sort of style. From how it frequently toggles back and forth between gameplay and mini-cutscenes, to the heavy metal BGM that goes hand-in-hand with the intensity of the action, to the badass freeze-frame approach to introducing new enemies (similar to how certain movies introduce characters, like a lot of Guy Ritchie / Tarintino flicks, both of whom I love). I also liked how in limbo, large text would appear in-world, often accompanied by a really low-pitched demon-voice growling it at you. It helped make it feel like the world itself had a sort of "♥♥♥♥ you" vibe, especially when it would be saying something like "STAY OUT" while the hallway you're in is suddenly stretched way out, with the floor pulling you away from the exit. Stuff like that was awesome.
Voice Acting? Check. I LOVED Dante's voice actor. Perfect fit voice-wise, and perfect line deliveries. Pretty much all of the voicework in this game was exceptional, though. From the supporting characters to the baddies, voices seemed to just fit really well.
Characters? Check. I'm huge on characters. A movie / book / game / etc. can be perfect in every other way, but if the characters suck I will have zero interest in it. The characters in DmC were all very solid, with Dante being flat-out magnificent. I'm pretty sure this game made me at least a little gay for him. Badass personality, voice, style, and he's hotter than the sun. It doesn't help that I already have an established weakness to demon-boys (Nightcrawler from X-Men, Rin from Blue Exorcist, Hellboy, etc). 10/10. What's not to love?
Plot? Check. I'm not religious, but I really love the whole angel and demons theme. It reminds me of something I remember Joss Whedon saying before, about how he's not religious either but still finds religious themes to be very intriguing and loves to incorporate them in his work. I also loved how no major plot-holes or deus ex machina elements jumped out at me. Everything fit really well, and the stuff that was slightly iffy got played off as tongue-in-check humor in most cases. If something seemed overly stupid or didn't make sense, Dante would immediately call it out. Instead of going along with everything immediately, he was often explained things or convinced of things before it would work out. Which I thought was fantastic. Overall, I would say the story itself was pretty straight-forward, but expertly handled.
All in all, I thoroughly enjoyed the game. Extremely happy with the experience, especially given my initial hesitation and expectations. This one is going down for me as an all-time favorite.
