You also get to compete in leaderboards. You know, all those hitman fans were just sitting around thinking that I was missing internet points to compete with my other friends in how many times I can get points in this game about points. That's why the first few hitman games had a giant point counter in the upper right corner of the screen. So, you knew you were getting them leet points. POINTS? Clearly someone missed the goddamn POINT of hitman. It's to be a HITMAN. Kill a target, get creative if you want, but you can just as easily use a sniper rifle to kill two targets with one bullet.
It was an accomplishment to have an elaborate or efficient kill. There wasn’t even an achievement in the old games for it, and the absolution achievements weren’t imposing about it either, they were just there if you figured out how to, for example, kill your target with the harpoon.

I get it, and lo and behold, there’s this thing called elusive targets.
One time missions that are time sensitive? The hell were you thinking? Hitman shouldn’t be a test of preparation and skill, no, we need one time content. That’s what people like. Not being able to play content. Or having to give up, I don’t know, a vacation or work or school or some other♥♥♥♥♥♥to make time to get your “GENIUS” idea for one time non-repeatable content? Really? God, the MOBILE hitman game was better.
Anyway, this is a horrible idea, a horrible package, and if you give them your money they will think that this is a good idea and they will continue to turn games into microtransactions either by butchering them like this and releasing them one limb at a time to your inbox or by having you literally pay to play. Wow... just wow! Just completed first playthrough of EGTTR... what an amazing concept. The graphics are just stunning, they maxed out my 980TI although apparently more optimisation is required but I didn't care when it got jerky occasionally as they were the best graphics I have EVER seen in a PC game... The cinematic music score is equally incredible and really rather haunting (best played on 7.1 headphones). This is not a game to rush through and there's no frantic action, more of a leisurely stroll exploring all the visual goodness that is available. The plot it pretty decent, still not sure I quite understand what happened here but I think that's kind of the point... Top tip - make sure you reach a save point before you quit though or you will lose your recent progress. If you want something you can dip into, lose an hour or two in a relaxing experience, this is definitely for you. That said, it does also build the tension quite nicely towards the end with the both the visual and audio atmosphere changing as the plot thickens. Is it the most exciting game I've ever played? No. Does it have the best graphics/audio score of anything I've played so far? Yes! Do I think it was money well spent, Yes. Would I buy it again/recommend it? Yes. Will I be playing it again. Yes! If you're in any doubt, just get it bought and give it a try, it does require some patience as it is NOT a fast paced game (although I believe a fast walk was availble on PS4 version, hopefully on this too) but to charge through it as fast as possible is to miss the point entirely... Anyway, enjoy!

This game very nearly made me cry at one point. This never happens. Games have a long way to go still.
But Everybody's Gone to the Rapture is one of the most beautiful digital experiences I've ever had.
The 'omg I might be welling up with emotion' point didn't occur during a scripted sequence, plot twist or revelatory event. No, my noticable emotional response happened somewhere in rural England in the empty household of a missing person, staring at a perfectly ordinary kitchen table, when suddenly the whole game- the world, the music, the setting, mood, sounds, the bumble bees- bloody EVERYTHING genuinely *got* to me.
The game is totally alien in design. You walk slowly. You look at stuff. You don't do a lot. And then... you realise that actually, yes you do. You *do* do a lot. You do so much in fact that I am in absolute awe of how every single aspect- even the shonky, radio drama quality of the dialogue - comes together in such a considered way.
This is a masterpiece of game design. You might wonder how I can say that so confidently when the game has no traditional gameplay. Get immersed. I swear on me mum I'm right.

The deep story is well hidden underneath layers of Call of Duty and when it finally completely surfaces, you're left contemplating every action you took, what it means to be a hero, and whether or not you're even sane.

This was a damn great game. Comparing this game to most other games just seems unfair. The story is amazing, the graphics are amazing, the sound is amazing and it all runs and looks very good on my slightly outdated rig. Nothing was done poorly save for the fact that the game has quite a few more bugs in it than would be desirable. If you have never played a game in the Arkham series than you will very much enjoy this game, although I would personally recommend going in order of release (Asylum, City then Origins). That all being said this game is both a prequel and a fairly stand alone story so you can play it out of order if you want.
Now, after all that being said let's get some context of where I think this game stands in the series by first stating what I think of the first two games. I consider Batman: Arkham Asylum to be one of the few perfect games ever made. That being said I didn't care for Arkham City all that much. I did still quite like it but I felt that Asylum did everything better. The downsides are that for one the combat feels slightly slower and easier, not by a whole lot but it is noticeable. Being that Asylum felt like it had a perfect difficulty I see this as a downside. Another is that the open world design of City felt unnecessary as you were still locked in an asylum like before but this time it essentially just had a large outdoor room connecting everything. In short it may have been technically open world but it wasn't very open and it wasn't very world either. Asylum however was spooky and claustrophobic and it just worked. Another issue with City was the story. City was all over the place in a way. In Asylum we mainly had the Joker and few other villains on the way and that was fine but with City it just couldn't keep its focus on who the main villain was. Also Asylum had one silly moment in regards to the last part of the game but City felt like it had many silly moments through out.
That all being said I would place this game just slightly under Asylum but above City. The combat is back to actually being somewhat difficult as it is sped up from City's slower combat. This kind of all goes out the window once you get a certain upgrade halfway through the game but even then I would hold Origin's combat above City's. Another thing done better is the city itself. For once in the series you actually get to be outside of an asylum's walls and actually stop crimes in progress and solve crimes and such. It actually feels like you are inside of a city which is further helped by about doubling the size of the map from City. Lastly is the story. My god, Origin's story just might be the best. We see a younger Batman who doesn't have much experience and is essentially going through his first significant night of crime fighting. There actually some character progression as opposed to Asylum or City where Batman was already experienced and is who he is. That all being said I would like to repeat as I said above, Origin's only real failing is that this game seems to be quite a bit more buggy than a game should be. I heard at launch it was even worse but even as it stands now I have enemies get stuck in walls making sections temporarily impassible. Nothing has happened that can't be fixed by reloading a checkpoint however so it doesn't detrack too much.
To sum everything up here:
Asylum: 100/100
City: 95/100
Origins: 99/100
P.S. Oh yeah, there is also a multiplayer but I never bothered to try it. It's designed by Splash Damage so chances are it's quite good but I bet no one plays it anymore.

What is ASTRONEER?
ASTRONEER is a space survival/exploration game. You are given the choice of 4 different player models to choose from before you are thrown onto a random section of an unknown planet. From there on out you choose what you must do to survive. Maybe you'll just wander off into the distance to explore until you inevitably die from a lack off oxygen. Or maybe you'll create a rover to wander even further off into the distance to explore until your rover inevitably runs out of power leaving you to die from a lack off oxygen, yet again. Or maybe you'll just get out your terrain tool and attempt to recreate that famous scene from the lion king by slowly ascending yourself into the sky whilst singing "Naaaaaaah Sevenya" only to run out of power and attempt to save yourself by jumping off and plummeting to your death. Or maybe you'll go through that whole ordeal and actually manage to survive, realising what a monstrosity of thing you've created, and call it "art".
In all seriousness, if you buy this game, please do keep in mind that this is an EARLY ACCESS game that the public has only recently been given access to, everything is subject to change and it is unoptimized despite what some people think meaning that yes, it's going to crash, yes, it's going to have large fps drops and yes, it's going to have game breaking yet hilarious bugs.
P.S: Or maybe you'll just buy this game to support the currently trending meme known as "YES MAN'S SKY"

I don't typically review games on Steam, but Astroneer has motivated me enough to do so. The game popped up on my suggested list, I looked through a few videos and screenshots and really enjoyed the artstyle so I thought I'd watch a couple Youtube videos of it. After 15 or 20 more minutes of consideration I decided to download it and give it a shot.
About two hours after first boot I'm completely smitten with the game. The basebuilding is handled elegantly. The general atmosphere of exploration is nice, and simply playing the game is enjoyable. For a something that just launched in Early Access I'm very hopeful for the future of the game. If more content and refinement of current systems is delivered I could very likely have a new favorite game on my hands.
As it is now, the gameflow goes about as such: Spawn in, find some resources, craft a couple things, build a couple buildings, get a vehicle, then start expanding your search area for more resources. You'll find researchable objects in points of interest on the planet, and bring those back to your base and research better tech.
It is simple now, and that's fine. I honestly like how little your hand is held when you start. I'm not one of those "Games are too easy!" folks, but I really enjoy the lack of UI elements on screen all the time, and the lack of talking head or floating boxes telling me what to do next really fosters an environment of discovery.
As I'm only a couple hours in I know I didn't get past the honeymoon period of stumbling upon a promising new game. I think if I had to attempt to see shortcomings in the game it would be a lack of variety in gameplay, and a certain point of feeling that you can no longer advance. That said, I have no idea how many technologies there are to research, and I know I haven't built a ship or traveled to another planet yet, so there is plenty more game for me to gleefully stumble blindly through.

I have spent quite a bit of time listening to people talk about how great this game was.  Prety much from the time of it's release many of my friends told me about how much fun it was.  Myself I cannot get past how awful the controlls are, and perhaps thats just a sign of a bad port to PC.  For a game that spends so much time driving you'd think the cars would be drivable, but the driving in this game is laughable.  It's more frustration than anything else, only being usable due to the lack of other cars on the road.  Most of the time the road either in your lane or oncomming trafic is clear so you don't have to worry about room to drive.  If you do happen to bump something the pinball collision bumpers will engage and through you completely off course, even if it's low speed bump against a light pole on your rear you may be sent spinning...
The on foot controlls are just as bad, most especialy the combat.  Being another major factor in the game play the guns and melee combat are horribly underdeveloped.  Aiming a gun using the mouse is clunky and less responsive than the original Doom.  The melee is just as bad making the melee in Morowind look like and advaced hand to hand combat simulator.
In several quest mandatory minigames I was left high and dry to figure out the controlls, and even worse durring at least one quest (Cesar Vialpando) the controlls were reversed to what the on screen prompts asked for.
One of the most frustrating things about this game is the save system.  In order to save a game you must return to your safe house... no mater how far away that safe house is.  It is simply absurd that there was not an option to save on the spot even if loading a save spawned the character at the safe house being forced to return there any tiem you want to save means that saving your progress could take five minutes or more.  Saving should not be an exercise in patience.
Finally, a big disapointment for me was the lack of anything interesting to do or see outside of listening to the radio and missions.  The city is very large, and well designed.  Driving around however it is just a bunch of buildings you can't enter  with NPCs milling about.  Occasionally you might hear a snip of conversation that may make you chuckle but the city is quite dull... whats the point of an open world sand box if there isn't anything to do.

Awesome LEGO game, and the same funny game as all the other LEGO ones. Plus, you can never go wrong with Batman!

When I first played this a few years ago, I didn't know too much about Batman. I didn't have to. This game serves as an excellent introduction to both the licensed LEGO titles by Traveler's Tales and the various interpretations of the Batman mythos from DC Comics, and if you're a fan of either, I'd be rather stunned if you didn't enjoy this.
It's your standard Batman plot. This one is not ripped from any existing film or comic, but is instead a new situation made to send you through as much of LEGO Gotham as it can, as both the Dynamic Duo of Batman and Robin shutting down the evil plans of Arkham Asylum's escaped supervillain denizens, and those iconic villains themselves going out to cause trouble. It's a very bright and colorful Gotham, though still quite dark. I guess it'd be more accurate to say it's a high contrast Gotham, and this leads to a rather gorgeous visual design heavily influenced by the Tim Burton films, a place that's beautiful when it's not being creepy as all heck.
It's much more the campy, silly kind of Batman than the darker Dark Knight of late (Arkham Asylum totally nailed that shortly after), though like I said, a few places are still certainly creepy. There are some changes for gameplay's sake, such as all of the villains being shipped off to Arkham Asylum (instead of some going to Blackgate Penitentiary, as Arkham is a hub level). Instead of constantly changing characters, the Hero missions have our heroes constantly changing Suits found within the level. Some are really cool, like the Glide Suit allowing you to soar or the Attract Suit allowing you to vacuum things (it's oddly entertaining), while others are just kind of a hassle or quickly forgotten about, like the Heat Protection Suit (good luck remembering it's a thing) or the Magnet Suit (have fun walking up walls very, very slowly every other level). You're able to switch between these as though they were separate characters in Free Play, and the villains don't have such gimmicks, so it kinda evens out in the end. You're able to unlock suit upgrades, and many of them, like speeding up the intolerably slow Magnet Suit to tolerable speeds, feel like they should've been available from the start.
The levels are very distinct, and for the most part, I would say very fun. This was, however, just before they started handling vehicles properly again in the LEGO games, so there are some completely infuriating moments where you have to tether your vehicle to mines and slam those mines into things, but they don't and they just slide around wildly until enemies blow them up and you have to start all over. When this is not the case, they are entertaining and explosive action sequences, but dang are they a pain to 100%. (Admittedly, I still boot up the game exclusively to play the Batmobile level, because you get to drive the Batmobile and just tear through the streets of Gotham.)
So, fans of the LEGO games, this was the game that set the par for the course, bringing in targeting mechanics, 32 levels, and a long list of increasingly obscure characters (Batman fans probably won't believe "Joker (Tropical)" made it into a "kid's game"). Fans of the Batman series, you'll find that much as the game takes liberties for the sake of humor or gameplay, they did really do their research first before intentionally making these choices. And you can play as Bane, Alfred, Batgirl, Nightwing, Hush, and one extra at 100% you're bound to geek out a bit over. Bios for each of the villains appear in the levels where the heroes fight them, so if you're new to the series and know very little about it, you'll come out quite well-learned.
All in all, it's fun. Campy, creepy, and stuffed to the gills with little nostalgic nods, atmospheric combat, and iconic characters. For once, it's exactly what it says on the tin. LEGO. Batman. There you have it. If that sounds good, go for it.

First off, It's not hard.
To make it hard you can adjust the options to your liking in the gameplay menu or get to level 20 to unlock professional mode.
Level 20.
You level up in a hitman game, and until you've completed the mission in a limited fashion you do not get access to OTHER WAYS to complete the mission. You want to put on a mascot outfit and samurai sword your targets through the head? Go for it. As a completionist, I forced myself to play the entire thing in order to get every single achievement, and even playing it casually, it was a painful experience.
is a puzzle game where you manipulate the sound in order to avoid enemies or remove what is blocking your path. It is a nice idea, but poorly executed. This review contain bits of the story that you would comprehend by playing it.
As I have mentioned before,
has an awesome idea behind: the majority of humans have decided to cover their eyes to hide themselves from the evils of the world, and you are a Seer - a person that decides to keep their sight, and therefore you are persecuted by the society. Enemies will hunt you through the sounds you make - and eventually, by your scent -, and you can activate or deactivate walls by screaming or by the sound of your footsteps. Great, isn't it?
Also, you find more about the story through the narrator every time you complete a level, and they have done a neat job with the voice acting.
It's great to add that this is a cheap game and I've seen it more than once on a 90% sale.
Hitboxes in this game are weird, so you'll see yourself hitting a lot of walls and then having to restart the whole puzzle. Talking about the puzzles, loads of them are unrewarding; I almost never felt that I had thought of something unthinkable, most of them involved only timing and running through places that looked like bug exploits.
Its achievements are all over the place. Some of them demand that you walk through every single leaf or piece of paper in the whole chapter, and this can easily bug and make you repeat a bunch of levels just so you can get it; others would require you not to die a single time during the whole chapter, and this would end up being extremely frustrating.
Even though the voice acting is nice, the Seer's voice isn't. His screams are hideous and playing with an headphone will easily give you a headache.
The Seer is slow, so a few easy levels end up taking forever to be completed. And the game is really repetitive, I was never able to play more than an hour at once without getting bored.
isn't a bad game, it just isn't as motivating and well executed as I wish it was. I can't fully recommend it because of the flaws I have pointed above, but I am sure that people can enjoy it more than I did.

While I recognize that the dev is a relative newcomer and that this product is a good try, I'm torn between giving a good or bad review.  I want indie devs to gain experience and I don't mind contributing to their efforts, but it's hard not to have a minimum standard of expectations.  Things that turn me off include lack of keymapping, lack of key remap function, lack of overhead map, lack of instruction of any sort, lack of plotline, making a pretty cover to a book that isn't there (no plot with good graphics), and just, plain bad games.  With almost anything else I can try to see the positives, but those things become tedious like tic tac toe.
This game treads on several of these put-offs, including all of the "lack" complaints mentioned.  As a pure FPS, to me, there is not enough action.  As an adventure game, to me, there is not enough plot.  As an exploration game, everything looks close enough to exactly the same that I'm bored by no scenery and there's no reason to "explore" sterile levels.
As a positive, the primary (only?) enemy (at least in early levels) are big, happy, pink bunnies that explode when you hit them... but that description is about as amusing as it gets even after you see it happen; it's the same thing every time.
FWIW, most of the FPS basic controls (LCTRL, E, space, LSHIFT, etc) are pretty normal, but anyone who knows this has already played games that will make them annoyed by playing this one instead of other, better games.
As a few positives
While I want to encourage the dev, I cannot endorse this product because I wouldn't send any of my friends to play it even if it were free.  That said, I did recieve the product for free from the below-mentioned source.

a good solid effort, but you chose FPS, a realm which is populated by a notoriously demanding following, and you didn't offer anything new - only proof that you could do it. Coming off of a pretty big Lego high after beating Lego Marvel Super Heroes I was quite excited to dive back into Lego Batman for the first time since it’s release. I had never beaten it back then so thought now would be a great time to do it. However, the game really hasn’t held up since it’s release in 2008.
The best thing about the Lego games is the cast of characters that you get to play as in each level that while obviously falling within specific archetypes are at least cool to see in Lego form and to control. Lego Batman has two playable characters in the Story mode - Batman and Robin. Instead of other playable characters they both get different suits which unlock unique abilities such as gliding as Batman or walking up magnetic walls as Robin. You can play as a multitude of characters in the free play mode but I have no idea why they went with the former in the story mode.
There are fifteen levels, most of which are your standard 3D platformer Lego fare with a handful of vehicle levels thrown in which adds a bit of variety to the standard formula. Each level has their a unique boss fight which more often than not I found to be uninspired with a very basic puzzle required to solve the fight. At least a good portion of Bat’s rogues gallery is here, Scarecrow; Two-Face; The Joker; Killer Moth etc. The levels themselves tend to be a lot of fun even if they all tend to look a little too similar due to the Gotham city backdrop.
I find Lego Batman really difficult to recommend with much better platformers and even better Lego games available. If you are looking for this specific type of game then try Lego Marvel, I have yet to play Lego Batman 2 but I hear that is a big improvement over this.

This reboot goes back to the roots of Blood Money in an episodic manner. So basically , they can make a  ton of content for it. The game's really well done , I spent 40 hours on the first and second episode. It has challenges that make the game even longer , it has escalation contracts that challenge you the more you complete it. You can always redo levels expect for Elusive Targets.
Graphics are great.
Gameplay is great.
Sound effects are great.
Voice acting for the main characters in the story line is great , but the NPCs acting will become repetitive. (not the dialogue , the voice. Same voice actors voice many other NPCs)
Sometimes , NPCs will be able to see through walls or with their backs turned at you , but it doesn't happen often and IO Interactive updates the game pretty often.
Besides the main story , there is Contracts mode which allows you to play or create a contract on the main story's levels. So basically you can make a random pedestrian in the street your target and create some conditions for it , like what disguise to wear , what weapon to use.
There are Elusive Targets , which disappear after some time and can only be performed once , and you have only one shot at it. So it's like a challenge on the run.
And for those who complain about Denuvo DRM , IO Interactive didn't have such a high budget like they did with Absolution so they have to combat piracy and get 1 year worth of sales.. give them a break. At least , they listen to the community by going back to Blood Money formula.

I absolutely loved this game! It's reasonably challenging without being super frustrating. The puzzles are really clever and thought-provoking, as is the general message. Is ignorance truly bliss? Or is it better to lose what may have once been a paradise for the chance to learn more. Definitely well worth a play! The challenges and achievements also offer a fair amount of replayability as you improve on the skills you learned.

Bottom line, there's no reason for me to be solving these puzzles. This type of game has the disadvantage of being unable to keep the player engaged by maintaining a good pace, since said pace is totally dependent on the player. Furthermore, in order to keep a person playing, a puzzle game needs one of two things (though preferably both): a good story/goal to motivate me to solve the puzzles or a sense of satisfaction from doing so. See No Evil lacks both. Up until the last two levels I played, it was mind bogglingly easy. The last two were plain frustrating. None made me feel that essential "eureka!" moment. There is simply no reward for being clever. Does it need to give me three star rating like some crappy phone game? No. An A+, million point score because I did my best? Of course not. But _something_ every once in a while would be nice. Maybe tell me why my character decided to see again or give some exposition as to what the hell is going on in this society. You know, something other than some vague narration (which is activaley discouraging me from progressing).
(Voice acting on the narration is nice, though. Gotta admit.)
The motivation you're supposed to have is you're trying to get to a mountain to scream in a horn and "wake up" all the people who decided to cover their eyes and live in blindness, which is apparently all of society. The problem here is twofold: first, while I might have been a little keen on saving the world at the start, that quickly changes when you discover that everyone wants to kill you. Second.... what? I spend the entire game sneaking around and trying not let enemies hear me so I don't get killed, just so I can then scream at them from a mountain? Maybe it's explained in the end, but I honestly couldn't force myself to care. I didn't play through the entire game because I wanted to make sure I could get my refund back, though I was halfway through chapter 3 out of 4 and I don't see it picking up that late into the game. Apparently there's a new game plus where there's more/tougher enemies, but if I could get through chapters 1, 2, and almost 3 in little over an hour, I can't see it taking much more than 4 hours to beat both ng and ng+.
The mechanics are interesting, but could use a little work. For example, there is an enemy that fears sound and moves away from it. This is implemented as a sound activated switch that consists of the enemy standing on a button and you having to scare it off in order to lower a barrier and progress. The enemy moves back onto the button after a couple seconds. I discovered, however, that walking so the enemy is no longer on screen freezes it so it won't step back on the button. Not knowing that you can actually keep it off the button makes two specific levels in chapter two unsolvable. I have looked online for solutions to those levels and they all use the same technique of freezing the enemy by leaving the screen.
There's ways for sound to travel diagonally by redirecting it through a sort of two sided megaphone, but you can't scream (i.e. make sound) diagonally. In order to use the megaphones that are diagonal you need to stand at a specific distance so that the expanding sound waves from your voice actually go through the funnel at a good enough angle to be registered.
The camera is glued to the player and you can't use it to look around, so often you have to (very slowly) walk over to what you want to see, look at it for a second, then (oh so slowly) walk back. I understand and agree with the choice of making the character's speed what it is as some puzzles would be completely broken if he walked much faster. Nevetheless, it would make the game much more enjoyable if you could just drag your mouse over to the edge of the screen to look a little farther, or control the camera a little with wasd if you're moving with the arrow keys. Something like that would remove a lot of unnecessary (and very slow) walking.
TL;DR: good idea, good narration. The mechanics need a little work. No motivation to play or keep playing whatsoever. It's not a terrible game, just not fun.

The game is one of the best management games I've played. This game might be complicated to some at first time. So it is better if you play the campaigns first. Campaign missions will guide you throgh all the basics of the game. After you get all the basics, the functions of this game will be a cakewalk.
When I first found this game, I did not like the 2D graphics and the complicated gameplay. Still I gave it a shot and slowly I started to like the game and now this is one of my favorite management games. Even the graphics looks really cute now even though I did not like it at first. The best thing is, the game is really small but higly addictive and fun.
This game is pretty realistic. Just like other simulation/management games, Prison Architect also forces you to THINK before you do any action. Even designing a prison can have bigger impacts later. This is where I failed most of the times in my first sandblox plays, thus ending up with issues like - angry prisoners starting riots because of starvation, prison staff getting tired, snitches getting caught and ending up dying, prisoners escaping which is because I placed large pipes under their cells making it easy for them to make tunnels etc. But these challenges are what make this game really interesting.
You don't really need a high end pc to run this game. However, when your prison starts to get big, you might face a lot of stutters and fps issues because of so many thing going on at the same time. I don't know if higer-end pc users gets this problem or not. This is the only issue that bothers me when my prison starts to get bigger.
So overall, if you like simulation/building/management games, this is for you. And if things get repetitive, then there is Escape Mode where you get to be a prisoner and find different tactics to escape the prison. There are tons of fun and creative maps made by other users which you can download and play this mode in or you can just build a prison and start playing escape mode in your own made prison. This game is a must have.

What is ASTRONEER?
ASTRONEER is a space survival/exploration game. You are given the choice of 4 different player models to choose from before you are thrown onto a random section of an unknown planet. From there on out you choose what you must do to survive. Maybe you'll just wander off into the distance to explore until you inevitably die from a lack off oxygen. Or maybe you'll create a rover to wander even further off into the distance to explore until your rover inevitably runs out of power leaving you to die from a lack off oxygen, yet again. Or maybe you'll just get out your terrain tool and attempt to recreate that famous scene from the lion king by slowly ascending yourself into the sky whilst singing "Naaaaaaah Sevenya" only to run out of power and attempt to save yourself by jumping off and plummeting to your death. Or maybe you'll go through that whole ordeal and actually manage to survive, realising what a monstrosity of thing you've created, and call it "art".
In all seriousness, if you buy this game, please do keep in mind that this is an EARLY ACCESS game that the public has only recently been given access to, everything is subject to change and it is unoptimized despite what some people think meaning that yes, it's going to crash, yes, it's going to have large fps drops and yes, it's going to have game breaking yet hilarious bugs.
P.S: Or maybe you'll just buy this game to support the currently trending meme known as "YES MAN'S SKY"

I usually dont write reviews, but if you're new to Counter-Strike and you are considering buying this game, PLEASE read this review. At almost 1000 hours, I would like to give my insight. (Which is a lot, sorry)
CS:GO is an amazing FPS that has mulitple modes, a new 2v2 mode (I actually really like this, it's basically competitve with less rounds and less people), a 10v10 mode (This is casual, mostly for screwing around and practicing), a Deathmatch (You basically choose your weapon and run around shooting people), a "War Games" (justifiably just a meme), and a 5v5 mode. Sounds pretty cool, right?! Well yes, they're all extremely fun to mess around with, have some fun, and play for a little while, maybe even play with friends. If you are not into games with a competitive scene, steer clear of 5v5, and I HIGHLY RECOMMEND THIS GAME TO YOU! It is very fun to play if you aren't playing it competitvely.
Now, that sounds great, unless you're a competitve gamer.
If you're looking for a game to play with a competitive scene, this game may SEEM like a great choice. The competitive mode (5v5) is a 30 round deathmatch, where you between Terrorists and Counter-Terrorists at 15 rounds, respawn at the beginning of each round. You need to balance your money and play to hurt your opponents money.
The last couple of sentences may make this look FANTASTIC. The problem is, IT IS, on paper. Once you get into the game, it is terrible to new players, as A LOT of people who play are on secondary accounts, in which their primaries have hundreds of hours (We call these smurfs, for future reference). This is met by these people wanting to kick you for "being a noob". People hack just because they can buy another account if they get banned, and people who are toxic just because they want to be. Yes, it is a game people take seriously, and for that reason, it can be hard for new players to enjoy their experience, and will have trouble ranking up and beyond, and it is even harder if you're solo. Unfortunately, the rest of this review doesn't get better.
The owner of Valve, Gabe Newell, has stated that the company isn't primarily a game company anymore, and they're focusing on other stuff now. Suffering because of this is their games like TF2 and CSGO, where staff and developer teams are limited. Due to these teams having their hands tied, guns are unbalanced, hackers still hack, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s and smurfs run rampid,  and hitboxes and hit registration are faulty. It is getting better in some aspects, but others, it continues to gain any progress.
In conclusion, this game could be the best FPS to ever be released, if only Valve put a little more love to it. It breaks my heart that this game can't reach it's full potential, hence my downvote. I will definitely change my recommendation once it gets to a bearable point, because i want this game to be as good as it can be. I highly recommend keeping an eye out for this game, maybe for Christmas we can have our old company back.

I don't typically review games on Steam, but Astroneer has motivated me enough to do so. The game popped up on my suggested list, I looked through a few videos and screenshots and really enjoyed the artstyle so I thought I'd watch a couple Youtube videos of it. After 15 or 20 more minutes of consideration I decided to download it and give it a shot.
About two hours after first boot I'm completely smitten with the game. The basebuilding is handled elegantly. The general atmosphere of exploration is nice, and simply playing the game is enjoyable. For a something that just launched in Early Access I'm very hopeful for the future of the game. If more content and refinement of current systems is delivered I could very likely have a new favorite game on my hands.
As it is now, the gameflow goes about as such: Spawn in, find some resources, craft a couple things, build a couple buildings, get a vehicle, then start expanding your search area for more resources. You'll find researchable objects in points of interest on the planet, and bring those back to your base and research better tech.
It is simple now, and that's fine. I honestly like how little your hand is held when you start. I'm not one of those "Games are too easy!" folks, but I really enjoy the lack of UI elements on screen all the time, and the lack of talking head or floating boxes telling me what to do next really fosters an environment of discovery.
As I'm only a couple hours in I know I didn't get past the honeymoon period of stumbling upon a promising new game. I think if I had to attempt to see shortcomings in the game it would be a lack of variety in gameplay, and a certain point of feeling that you can no longer advance. That said, I have no idea how many technologies there are to research, and I know I haven't built a ship or traveled to another planet yet, so there is plenty more game for me to gleefully stumble blindly through.

I feel like I ought to have more to say about Spec Ops: The Line. Or, er, maybe Spec Ops feels like I ought to have more to say about it, cuz boy, does it try to goad you. It fails, naturally, as it constantly tries to serve 2 audiences at once with its conventional cover-based shooting (you know, for the normies) threaded between an antagonistic and thoroughly friggin oblivious morality play about the way gaming cheapens the horrors of war (you know, for the ***holes.) And for those of you who do manage to make it to the final scenes without feeling like youve just been condescended to by a vomiting english lit major who just got a copy of godel escher bach for their birthday, Spec Ops throws a little Bioshock "gotcha" bs in there for good measure. Spec Ops is the frat boy intellectual of videogames, so make room and get the solo cups, everybody.
Which is a pisser, as it almost works as contemporary spec (ops) fiction: taking place in a war-decimated version of Dubai, the setting offers a peek at what a ruined society might look like once what we know to be prosperity finally loses its balance. It makes for a fascinating playground, playing cowboys and indians among beached catamarans and formerly resplendent skyscrapers buried beneath tons of sand and ruin. For those of you who are wondering why Im recommending a game that Im also trashing, its this caveat: production design is mesmerizing. Spec Ops: The Line occupies a believably precarious world that deserves a bit more exploration and when the game gets itself together enough to know when to shut the hell up, it can offer up one of modern gaming's most unique dramatic experiences. But damn if it doesnt yammer on - uh, like I'm doing right now. Huh, I guess I did have something to say about it.

After almost a thousand hours of my life got sucked into this game, I thought it'd be a good time to review this beautiful piece of software that is ETS2.
Let's get this obvious out right away, if you do not like trucks, highways or european scenery then you'll definitely want to stay out of it. But then again, the amazingly relaxed gameplay might be just what you need to take the edge off after a long and stressful day of work.
I know right! Who would want to drive "aimlessly" in a video game when real life's already a drag... That's where you'd be wrong.
As odd as it sounds, driving a 25-tons vehicle through highways and narrow roads is the most relaxing and relieving activity I've ever found to counter life's burden and anxiety on a daily basis.
You heard right, I play this game almost everyday, may it be only for an hour or twelve!
If you have an addiction tendency and are trying to fight it,
As you'll most likely loose all social interactions with your peers. Family, friends, coworkers and boy/girlfriend will always come second with this game (close second maybe but second nonetheless).
Nothing will stop you from getting in your truck and getting those trailers on the road.
If I'm being perfectly honest, you should know that I only played vanilla for a month before I started modding the s*** out of this game. And I'm telling you, there is no end to the possibilities with the truly outstanding modding community that is out there (I'm obviously talking about modders themselves, not the end-users).
If you're not into modding (well you'll be) it's your lose. Map extensions, trucks, trailers, AI models and behaviour, sounds, weather, graphics, plug-ins and even an unofficial mp... Don't get me wrong, SCS made a wonderful product, but modders gave it its heart.
I'd never thought I would say this one day, as I wasn't that much of a truck enthusiast, but this trucking game is the best game I've ever been into! Sure it's not an fps or a fast-paced race game, but it's an adventure in and of itself.
Be a self-made trucker, haul thousands of tons and explore Europe from top to bottom, I dare you.
P.S.: I'm not biased, I'm in love...

sadly after thinking hard about it, im going with a no on this one.
since everyone has talked about the online-only thing(which is also a factor) ill skip on to what else is in the game;
stuff i like:
+the world feels much more immersive. conversations, oppertunities and the "preplanning" add much to the world surrounding the mission
+custom user-generated missions add replayability to the missions(going beyond trying to earn all achievements and such)
+stealth feels much more necessary and guns blazing tactics are much harder to pull off, demanding more careful planning
stuff i dislike/why im voting no:
-the games performence; an issue in and of itself. my gear may not be at the top but im well above the minimum requirements so the game shouldnt stutter on low, and it seems im not the only one getting this.
-shooting feels awkward, changing sensitivity in the menu seems to hardly have had enough impact, and moving my cursor while in aim mode is hellishly slow
-while i was excited for being capable of melee takedowns and specialized *weapon eliminations*(double tap with pistols, knife kills and such) it died out fast when melee combat became more QTE than fights, during which you are locked in place and cannot move/cut out of the slugfest
-enemies can no longer friendly fire at each other. unlike in many older hitman games, where enemies could also hurt each other, this time they can only hurt you(and some props). combined with how melee fights work out, a group of 3 enemies would spray you dead through each other, thanks to the bullets phasing through their *friend* in a slugfest with you
and lastly(this is mostly a nitpicky thing of mine): a leaderboard isnt really what i want in a singleplayer game.
while the game has its good points, i feel that at the price i paid and for what little of it i actually got to enjoy(much of my time on record is afk time from having to get up mid-game), i cant fully recommend it. adding to it the online only features(which, yes, we can now play offline but unlocks and challanges still seem to not be there for you when and if you want to play offline), i'd say if you want to give this game a spin you should wait for a sale.

This is a slow, terrible and cumbersome first person shooter mod for Half Life 2 that feels like a hardcore version of Left 4 Dead. Your multiplayer co-op party needs to carry out objectives in maps and mostly just stay alive. Its pretty easy to stay alive and not die, but its difficult to do anything else. First of all, the game is pretty slow. I mean the animations of your character are slow. When you switch to a flash light, it is always off to start with, then you need to turn it on.... WITH BOTH HANDS! Watch as your character slowly turns on a flashlight with his left hand while holding it with his right. Then there's the inventory system that has a good use of space management. The catch is that you really can't hold all that much. Your ammo takes up space, which is logical, its just I can't imagine when it comes down to carrying a sledge hammer, flashlight and a rifle that you can't carry all three at once.
You walk pretty slow (there is a sprint button), which is okay, but you swing pretty slow and the zombies shuffle their way toward you. Oh and when you get bitten, its like a poison that will slowly drain your health until you're dead. Once you're dead, your character becomes a zombie while you spectate as a ghost. Reloading takes quite a while, but maybe other video games have spoiled me into reloading fast when the reality is that it takes a while.
Carrying things is a chore, don't drop a key next to a door, because you'll never be able to pinpoint the key on the ground from the door. Maps have invisible walls preventing exploration, even when it looks like there is exploration.
Another downside is, this isn't really a campaign, its just more of a series of multi player co-op maps. Left 4 Dead is just better. There's a reason why this took 2 years to make it to Steam. Its just a cumbersome game and maybe that adds to the survival horror aspect, but eh its not for me. This isn't an action game, its a slow beast walking toward you when you can't reload your rifle fast enough.

I bought this game mainly because of the setting - 1980's England.  I was thinking it would be an interesting game to walk around in such a time and experience such a story.  But for me after the initial joy of walking around the village it became rather detached and dull.  I understand it is game based on the rapture, so finding people is unlikely task I will complete.  But by walking around (painfully slow) and just listening to people’s lives.  There isn't that two-way communication like the other isolated style game of Firewatch.  I assumed with a rapture based game there would at least a few 'left behind' if this was indeed going to be a rapture in the biblical sense, but it wasn't.  The music was lovely, the graphics excellent, but I felt very detached from the game.  More like watching a TV programme than being in it.  And I would recommend anyone interested in this game just looking on YouTube on one of the many ‘Let’s Play…’ videos.  It will be the same thing.
I do hope the game developers continue with the 1980’s England theme in another game, I really do.  I would love to see perhaps a murder-mystery (maybe even a bit like Hot Fuzz!) or perhaps some cold war conspiracy similar to Tinker Tailor Solider Spy or the Fourth Protocol.

The game is one of the best management games I've played. This game might be complicated to some at first time. So it is better if you play the campaigns first. Campaign missions will guide you throgh all the basics of the game. After you get all the basics, the functions of this game will be a cakewalk.
When I first found this game, I did not like the 2D graphics and the complicated gameplay. Still I gave it a shot and slowly I started to like the game and now this is one of my favorite management games. Even the graphics looks really cute now even though I did not like it at first. The best thing is, the game is really small but higly addictive and fun.
This game is pretty realistic. Just like other simulation/management games, Prison Architect also forces you to THINK before you do any action. Even designing a prison can have bigger impacts later. This is where I failed most of the times in my first sandblox plays, thus ending up with issues like - angry prisoners starting riots because of starvation, prison staff getting tired, snitches getting caught and ending up dying, prisoners escaping which is because I placed large pipes under their cells making it easy for them to make tunnels etc. But these challenges are what make this game really interesting.
You don't really need a high end pc to run this game. However, when your prison starts to get big, you might face a lot of stutters and fps issues because of so many thing going on at the same time. I don't know if higer-end pc users gets this problem or not. This is the only issue that bothers me when my prison starts to get bigger.
So overall, if you like simulation/building/management games, this is for you. And if things get repetitive, then there is Escape Mode where you get to be a prisoner and find different tactics to escape the prison. There are tons of fun and creative maps made by other users which you can download and play this mode in or you can just build a prison and start playing escape mode in your own made prison. This game is a must have.

Going in, I really wanted to enjoy this game. The synopsis was fascinating, and the reviews were mostly positive. I somehow had it figured for the next
. But after playing it, I can only picture
working as more of a free internet flash game than something I would pay actual money for.
is a puzzle game primarily, not the story-rich fable I had gone in expecting. A series of vague, proverbial journal entries from a book you find next to a dead man offer supposed clues to the puzzles you face in each room, and a female narrator occasionaly remarks on your journey as you progress from room to room. As far as I can tell, that is about the extent of
. The gameplay is unbalanced and frustrating. The music and sound design choices are strange, questionable and, at times, uninspired. For example, your character uses sound to navigate and activate parts of the puzzles. While this is an interesting concept, his scream ("Loh!") gets old quite quickly. Simply adding a few variations of his scream could have alleviated this. An example of unbalanced gameplay is that your avatar moves much slower than your enemies, making them nigh on impossible to avoid when they detect you, and as soon as they do catch you, you must start the puzzle all over, regardless of the progress you may have made. The only checkpoints are at the start of the level. The puzzles, might I add, can become very tedious, and the prospect of starting one over after making a considerable dent in one does not appeal to me very much.
Despite all this, I did enjoy the visual aesthetic of
--the style minded me of
--and it did seem like there was an interesting story hidden in there somewhere. However, from a very early point this game failed to catch my attention or stroke my curiosity enough to overcome these shortcomings. All it has done thus far is frustrate, confuse, and dissapoint me, and for these reasons I cannot in good conscience recommend
. I shall continue to play, perhaps with the assistance of a walkthrough, but at this point I doubt my oppinion will change.

As a fan of the series for maybe 14 years Hitman is one of my top games of 2016.
It wasn't apparent at first just how much there is to do, every mission has about a dozen paths already laid out with objective markers and clues, and it's fun to experiment whether you just follow the crumbs or turn off the guidance and let yourself mess up on occasion. Messing up is actually part of the magic, and it's not without frustration but failing can be fun in Hitman.
Eventually you decide to go off path and dispatch of the targets your own way, then you realise there are just as many options the game doesn't tell you about at all, indeed they're probably easier than those the game suggests. You'll replay missions over and over trying different approaches, either to get achievements or just for fun. Then you'll go on Youtube and realise there are things you can do you never noticed, not because they're secrets, just because you never considered looking for them.
Then you have Contracts, Escalation and Elusive Targets. The quality is hit-and-miss but I've had great excitement, fear and joy playing them and I appreciate that the devs have been able to experiment with the formula and create some awesome moments in the process.
There are things about the game which nobody is happy about, they have definitely effected me from time to time. Some have been improved yet there is still more that could be done, but Hitman's negatives are almost inconsequential to it's positives and IO have built not only a great game but a great system for delivering more missions and new types of content in the future.
Hitman gets to the core of the franchise while stretching the entertainment well past anybody thought it could be stretched to, and throughout the whole experience it manages to match or exceed expectations. And they're still working on it.

This is a slow, terrible and cumbersome first person shooter mod for Half Life 2 that feels like a hardcore version of Left 4 Dead. Your multiplayer co-op party needs to carry out objectives in maps and mostly just stay alive. Its pretty easy to stay alive and not die, but its difficult to do anything else. First of all, the game is pretty slow. I mean the animations of your character are slow. When you switch to a flash light, it is always off to start with, then you need to turn it on.... WITH BOTH HANDS! Watch as your character slowly turns on a flashlight with his left hand while holding it with his right. Then there's the inventory system that has a good use of space management. The catch is that you really can't hold all that much. Your ammo takes up space, which is logical, its just I can't imagine when it comes down to carrying a sledge hammer, flashlight and a rifle that you can't carry all three at once.
You walk pretty slow (there is a sprint button), which is okay, but you swing pretty slow and the zombies shuffle their way toward you. Oh and when you get bitten, its like a poison that will slowly drain your health until you're dead. Once you're dead, your character becomes a zombie while you spectate as a ghost. Reloading takes quite a while, but maybe other video games have spoiled me into reloading fast when the reality is that it takes a while.
Carrying things is a chore, don't drop a key next to a door, because you'll never be able to pinpoint the key on the ground from the door. Maps have invisible walls preventing exploration, even when it looks like there is exploration.
Another downside is, this isn't really a campaign, its just more of a series of multi player co-op maps. Left 4 Dead is just better. There's a reason why this took 2 years to make it to Steam. Its just a cumbersome game and maybe that adds to the survival horror aspect, but eh its not for me. This isn't an action game, its a slow beast walking toward you when you can't reload your rifle fast enough.

HITMAN™ is really, really good. It blends the great stuff from Hitman: Absolution such as the improved combat and graphical fidelity with the traditional hardcore stealth elements of classic instalments such as; Hitman 2: Silent Assassin and the infamous and well-loved Hitman: Blood Money.
It lets you approach objectives anyway you want to; whether that be never being detected and only killing your targets or going completely guns blazing.
Enix gives you seven missions, (that may not seem like a lot but just keep reading I will say why it is ok) that are all spread across different parts of the world;
-ICA Facility: this is your training stage.
-France (Paris): this is at a massive home where a fashion show is currently taking place.
-Italy (Sapienza): this is a small little town on the coast of Italy with a mansion that you have to infiltrate.
-Morocco (Marrakesh): this is a city currently under military control giving you an even harder job at completing your mission.
-Tailand (Bangkok): this takes place within a hotel resort along the coast; due to it being in a hotel resort it has lots of things the targets can do to seek pleasure such as massages, this gives you loads of opportunities to kill them in a variety of ways.
-USA (Colorado): this is within a small rural town. This is an interesting mission in itself because you can play that stalker like role within the cornfields and pretend to be scarecrows pinned up.
-Japan (Hokkaido): and finally this is set in an extremely high tech tower facility thousands of feet above sea level.
Now you may be thinking: "These missions don't sound interesting at all mate..."
In which my response is: "Words do not do the mission design any justice."
Going back to the idea that seven levels aren't a sufficient amount for a full priced AAA game. This game centers its longevity and replayability around one thing VARIETY. Whether that be as simple as mixing your playstyles up between levels or trying to master one level with all the weapons and strategies possible making you a 'Silent Master Assassin'. The game's beauty like all the other so called 'Hitmen' games comes in mastering the levels so you know them by the back of your hand no matter the size of them so you feel like you know each targets movement cycles and where to go to kill them with certain things; practically making yourself as proficient as possible at killing HVTs.
The missions are not only just on their lonesome. You have the standard missions of course with literally dozens of mastery challenges to complete but you also have things called 'Escalation Contracts' which place you in the same mission but give you different targets within them such as a particular high ranking security guard or a private investigator. In addition to this, there is also complete revamped versions of the standard missions you get, for example; in Sapienza there is a mission where you have to kill an actor while he is on set shooting a new movie. (This occurrence is not happening in the standard mission by the way).
So, like I said the game prides itself on it's replayability and value for money. It's quality over quantity but the latter half is not lacking at all. They blended the quality of content with the amount of content well.
It is worth noting the graphics are fantastic, the gameplay is fun; you don't die too quickly like in some games but you don't take that many bullets to be taken down (it's realistic and authentic), the story is kind of hit or miss for me; if you are a die hard Hitman fan (and you haven't already bought it) you may dig it - it's very simplistic and barebones but it gets the job done so it's fine.
All in all, definitely worth picking up!

See no evil Review - Raymond KT
See No Evil is a ridiculously engaging, unconventional sound-based puzzler developed by a small team at Noetic Games that blends original and challenging gameplay with a thought-provoking premise. It just dropped on Steam for $15 after a successful Kickstarter campaign earlier this year, and sports a surprising amount of polish.
Players are abruptly dropped into a discomforting alternate reality where humanity has sworn off sight and progress in favor of comfort and consistency. Voluntarily shutting their eyes, ostensibly for generations, the protagonist opens his when a body crashes through the roof. Belonging to another Seer, as the dissidents are known, the late individual’s journal is read, line by line, as players advance through the initial set of levels. He must use his newly-acquired sight to escape the dystopian realm.
See No Evil is a dark, isometric puzzle game about sound manipulation. A harsh fantasy where the willingly blind are hostile to the nonconformist. Sometimes, the world seems darker with your eyes open. Unfinished, unpolished game. Several bugged achievements and a nice big crash when quiting the game. Maybe you are lucky and Alt + F4 works. Otherwise you have to restart. Great work. Beside that? Graphics are freaking scary. Our hero looks like a cartoonish LSD version of our beloved witcher Geralt. Musics are good, sounds are basically screams.

I'm going to be unpopular opinion puffin and I'm
going to recommend this game. I finished the 'definitive edition' of the game, which means that it should be the least buggy and most balanced version with the most stuff to do - i.e. it should be the best the developers can offer. However, despite the name ("definitive") this version was not much different from the first, albeit with only 1 extra hour's worth of content thrown in.
Moving on, first I will talk about the bad things, seeing as I am not recommending it, and then I will talk about the good.
Firstly the bad:
1. Short Length - The game is only about 9 hours long if you want 100% completion rate. I finished the game with 100% completion in exactly 9 hours 21 minutes and 24 seconds. So for what it was, I finished it completely in 2 sittings.
2. No Replay Value - After finishing the game 100% and collecting everything, there is literally nothing else to do except hunt down a couple of pesky achievements. I managed to get over 75% of them in just a single playthrough and I could probably get most of the others in under an hour if I was bored enough as most just involve killing enemies enough times with a certain skill.
3. The Price - Given the game costs $20, takes only barely 9 hours to beat casually 100% and has no replay value. I think that it's somewhat expensive. Hollow Knight took me over 50 hours to get 100% completition in, and had 10x the variety and depth. Not only that, it's 25% cheaper.
4. Performance - I actually found the game lagged a bit at critical moments which made me die a couple of times. It wasn't such a big deal, but I wasn't impressed with the fact that there's no way to customise the graphical options. Having said that, I shouldn't have to because my machine cost over $3000 and I can play games with far better graphics that do not lag at all. The frame rate did spike enough times to warrant me mentioning it.
5. Enemy variety - Ori and the Blind Forest has very little variety in enemies. There's about 12 or so enemies total. Blobs, bigger blobs, rhino things, frogs that spit, jumping frogs, spiders, spitting tentacles, balls of energy that fire lazers and owls. That's pretty much it entirely. There's really no other enemies in the game, and instead of making new enemies they just recloured each enemy at least once to signify it being stronger. For comparison Hollow Knight had over 80 different enemy types, not even including the 20 or so bosses and both had lots of mehcanics that had to be learned.
6. Boring Combat - Basically a light follows you and you just mash attack to shoot auto-guided lightning at enemies. You can shoot from safe distanes or behind cover. There's really little skill involved. Upgrading your attack just increases the range and damage. You do get a few other skills like a stomp etc, but your other skills have more movement and environmental usage than combat usage. Oh and you get way too much health. 15 energy and life at the end which is a crazy amount even on hard.
7. Platforming Issues - Some parts of the platforming are really bad. Granted, a lot of bugs were fixed from the original version and the platforming is WAY better on this version. However, I still felt that some parts were unncessarily stupid and at times (and even with all skills) it was just too easy to fail a task by just an inch or split second. In addition to this, I didn't like the addition of a few areas that were only 1-way.  Ex. Ginso Tree and the right area in Black Root Burrow.
--------------------------------------------------------------
All in all the game was pretty good and features some of the best music of any game and a really beautiful story. However. compared to other metroidvania/platformer games. I felt a bit let down after realising that a casual playthrough could completely finish it in under 10 hours. I have to compare it to similar games like Hollow Knight, and maybe if I hadn't played games like 'HN' I'd be able to recommend OATBF, but for the price and given the above issues, I can't recommend it.
It's fun for a good portion of the 9 hours, but at times it's frustrating and finishing it left me feeling disappointed in the depth, variety and length. Buy it if it's about $10 bucks. That's my honest opinion.

Elves Adventure is stunning. It's not bad in the traditional way games are bad. It's not frustrating, the story is barely there to criticize, and it doesn't even necessarily feel unfinished. Rather, Elves Adventure is bad because it feels like it was constructed by a child. Seriously, it reminds me of the maps I made in Starcraft when I was 8. It has all of the same problems that my maps had: Huge, mostly empty levels, alternate paths that lead to nothing, random and disproportionate item placement, and so on. It's the hallmark of inexperience with game making, and of playing games in general.
Elves adventure also reminds me of my past self's maps in how it solves its gameplay problems. The "solutions," if you can call them that, are an afterthought at best, barely solving the problem without a moment to consider what problems the "solution" will generate. Want a part of the level to be in shadow? put an opaque black texture over it. Want to make sure the player knows they're injured? Put a barely-translucent red filter over the screen with an overly-loud heartbeat sound, even if they're still mostly at full health. The level design also puts a lot of trust in the player. It trusts us to follow the path and find the only spots of content on the map. During the boss fights, it trusts us to stay and shoot the boss to death, not just walk past it to the exit. It trusts us to know that a monster is supposed to
a boss fight, because they're in the back. It takes a little imagination to see a complete game.
The plot is also childlike in its earnestness. It gives you mission after mission, some of which are in the game, some of which are not. The main goal of the game is to get to your home planet, which is apparently very important. Then at the end you can choose to not go back? I'm not sure how that choice is supposed to be meaningful at all, since nothing about that choice is explained. Nothing in this game is explained. Anyway, the tone is nonexistent. It starts in a happy cartoon forest level, then goes to a set of spooky horror levels, then a set of nondescript volcano(?) levels. Why? I'm tempted to give the story a pass because of the charming sincerity it has, but it's got a long way to go before it becomes an actual narrative.
Also, I'm pretty sure all of the assets are shamelessly ripped from other games, at least the weapons. Naughty.
I want to close by addressing the developer. Patryk, if you're reading this, don't let the negative response to this game discourage you. You're probably pretty young, I'd guess 14 or under, and it's great that you're passionate about your hobby. The dungeon and graveyard levels had some pretty decent atmosphere, so I know you have talent. However, I hope you understand that this game isn't ready for a release like this. Keep practicing, and put your games somewhere like itch.io. Then, someday you can release something on steam that everyone will love. I believe in you.

The Archers meets Quatermass!!
The year is 1984 and a rural english villiage has been isolated by the Government due to a bizzare form of Ebola Sickness.  Also secret Experiments with  Space Telescope Radio Waves has brought to Earth a strange Alien Lifeform that takes the shape of Light Waves which  seem to have intelligence.  This life form is invading living humans reducing them to Atoms!!  For some  strange reason it is also converting their Clothing and property which is something the Programmers overlooked no doubt. The only signs of any "Human" life within the exclusion zone are radio transmitions by creepy Number Stations. All we know is that the player is being lead around by an Orb of Energy that replays the last moments of certain individuals lives....but is it here to help or to destroy?
This is a very enjoyable and relaxing experience that slowly gets more and more creepy as we progress.  There are a number of elements borrowed from the Tin Foil Hat conspiracy theorists that are fun to unpack and explore.  Fans of old 1950's SciFi movies such a Villiage of the Dammed and The Bodysnatchers will love this...
But it also has it's problems.  Most notably this game only allows the Player just One Profile and One profile only.  Secondly with this in mind the Game locks you in on the seconmd to last level.  This means that if there is any story you have missed or places you want to explore then Tough, you will just have to restart the game and do the whole things again from the beginning - a very annoying feature to say the least.
Thirdly, and this is the real kick in the pants, is that this game dosen't have an actual ending to speak of, it just stops and thats that.  If you are expecting the "Grand Finale" of Dear Esther or the "Full Circle" of Amnesia then you are not going to get it here.  Even after being very careful to visit all the locations, to unlock all the conversations, listen to all the radio signals and telephone calls, switch on all the TV's (and make notes of the number sequences).....Heck I even played with the Train Set and Rode the Witches Hat....The final "Character" level is extremely short and then the game....well....just sort of "Ends".  In Fact one gets the distinct impression that the Team were very pushed for time and had to wrap things up in a hurry for a release date. I hope there will ba a patch or an update sometime because we, as well as the game itself, really should have an ending - even if it's an obscure one.

If you like Dear Esther and/or Adr1ft then you will surely love Rapture.
If you've never played a "walking sim" and are expecting something resembling "regular" gameplay then you could be dissapointed.
The amount of detail poured into this idyllic English countryside setting is simply jaw dropping. The musical score, story and voice acting are all superb.
If your English then imagine a really interesting episode of "The Archers" or a non-comedy episode of "Dirk Gently" (both are radio shows) and you have an idea of the production quality of the story and voice acting, which lend themselves to feeling like you're actually listening to a radio show.
Ever since Dear Esther i have wanted something similar but on a much grander scale, Rapture has certainly scratched that itch, but (and maybe it's because im English and have wandered many a countryside village) after it ended i was left a tiny bit dissapointed at the lack of any caves or hidden nooks and crannies, actual places that make you go "oooooh" like dear esther did, rather than just relying on the detail and advanced graphics.
Overall i can reccomend this game to people who already know they enjoy walking sims, this is the best there is and any/all negative points i have made above are because i wanted to write a balanced review and not just gush about the 5 hours i spent in game :D
If you've never been completely sold on walking sims then this would be the one over all else that could possibly change your mind, especially if you like being told a good story where you feel like your peicing it together yourself, but you'll probably feel like you paid more than you should.
TL/DR:
Love walking sims? Then this is highly reccomended even at full price.
Not so fond of walking sims but like the look/story of Rapture? Then remember you have 2 hours to try it out, should get you through the first 2 "chapters", if it's not for you then no probs bob, get your refund, otherwise you'll probably feel more at home picking this up on sale at 40% off or more.

In short, one of the greatest games of all time, for any system, and really a 'must play' for FPS solo or co-op fans (especially small group co-op fans but also for those of us who prefer solo play).
Combines excellent game play, a well integrated leveling system, a scaling challenge level done better than most other games (a wee bit repetative originally but at this points all the DLC content eases that issue), and a loot reward system that has a near perfect amount of grind vs. joyous moments when an upgrade drops. The storyline is hilarious and the mythos at this point is one of the best in modern gaming.
The characters and the playstyles... they give the game play almost infinite replayability because a melee based assassin is radically different from a support Soldier which is different than a tanking Berzerker which is in turn different than a pet centric Mechromancer, etc. etc. etc. Perhaps most importantly, they're all FUN. I've got 1 main and 1 serious alt, and 4-5 other alts I play on occasion, and they all handle groups or the big fights solo differently. Obviously this all leads to even more variey in coop teams on the high end, as how you intergrate those character and playstyle/power tree combos changes so much.
The only flaws, and they're miniscule and not even an issue to everyone but I'll list them for detail, are melee being a bit challenge to intergrate on PC mouse/keyboard compared to console (experienced players or people willing to spend $ for a PC controller or button heavy mouse overcome this), the inability to customize characters, no female soldiers, no male Sirens, no hispanic mechromancer, no ... whatever Zero is, alien? robot? aug human?... Psychos (which is offset by a ton, a digital ton, of outfits, heads and vehicle skins and offset by the demands of the voice acting and story), the occasional minor preachiness on homosexuality (which is only a problem if it's a problem for you, the Devs integrated it damn well into the story!, Pandora is like 80-85% male and started as sort of work prison after all, those guys had to like dudes or like skags), and minor plot holes (offset by the humor, some Dev clarification out of game, and otherwise INSANELY engaging writing).
OVERALL: A 9.5+ of 10, easily. Depending on preference a 10 or 11. ;)
Also check out the "pre"-sequel (a decent game in it's own right, essentially a slightly improved massive DLC story), Tales from the Borderlands (epic storytelling game), and let's all hold out for Borderlands 3 sometime in '16-'17 :)

APB: Reloaded, a game where Pay-to-win is not optional but mandatory. I have some good and bad points that I would like to share with you but first you may notice my hours on the game don't seem like I have much experience. I can assure you that I have been playing APB: Reloaded for over 3 years now.
Anyway, onto the good points, this game has a wide-range of customisation options for pretty much anything from weapons to cars and everything inbetween (Mostly just cars, characters and weapons though). The wide array of customisation is what seperates the GTA (Grand Theft Auto) styled game from others such as APB: Reloaded.
As for the game itself it has a sort of "unique" fighting style as a shot from a weapon does the same damage to the foot as it would to the head which draws in a much more casual audience who would prefer this fast-paced massive open world of carnage and mayhem. There are all kinds of different weapons in APB; High Velocity, SMG's, Rifles, Stun guns, Pistols, LMG's and even High Explosive weapons featuring the OSMAW (RPG type weapon) and OPGL (Grenade Launcher). This open-world environment is ideal for the casual gamer who's looking to get a "thrill" in playing something like GTA, just without the cost.
Anyway, this game can't be all good and fun. As mentioned in my first paragraph, the developers rely a lot more on the money in their pockets rather then upgrading the game a lot faster. APB: Reloaded is heavily pay-to-win which in the end forces you to hand over your money to get something a lot more powerful in-game.
With my personal experiences in APB, they have probably one of the worst Anti-Cheat systems around, also known as punkbuster. Random kicks on innocent players and one of the slowest anti-cheat detectors allows hackers to walk right into the game and play as they would a normal player.
This is where I end, I could go on and on about the bad things that happen in this game but I would prefer for you to try it out, and just a quick warning. It can get highly addictive, incredibly fast.

Euro Truck Simulator 2 (commonly abbreviated as ETS2) is a vehicle simulation game developed and published by SCS Software for Microsoft Windows, Linux and Mac OS X and was initially released as open development on 19 October 2012. The game is a direct sequel to the 2008 game Euro Truck Simulator and it is the second video game in the Truck Simulator series. The player can drive one of a choice of articulated trucks across a depiction of Europe, picking up cargo from various locations and delivering it. As the game progresses, it is possible for the player to buy more vehicles, depots, and hire drivers to work. The game has sold over 4.9 million units as of September 2016.
